name: Kellie Castle
why_interesting: A beautifully preserved National Trust castle with remarkable painted ceilings.

name: Rossend Castle
why_interesting: The picturesque ruins of a medieval tower house overlooking the Firth of Forth.

name: Borthwick Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Borthwick Castle is one of the largest and best-preserved surviving medieval Scottish fortifications. It is located twelve miles (19 km) south-east of Edinburgh, to the east of the village of Borthwick, on a site protected on three sides by a steep fall in the ground.
why_interesting: One of Scotland's best-preserved medieval castles, still operating as a luxury hotel.

name: Castle of Mey
Wikipedia Extract: The Castle of Mey (also known for a time as Barrogill Castle) is located in Caithness, on the north coast of Scotland, about 6 miles (10 km) west of John o' Groats. In fine weather there are views from the castle north to Orkney.
why_interesting: The former holiday home of the Queen Mother overlooking the Pentland Firth.

name: Dounreay
Wikipedia Extract: Dounreay (; Scottish Gaelic: Dùnrath) is a small settlement and the site of two large nuclear establishments on the north coast of Caithness in the Highland area of Scotland. It is on the A836 road nine miles (fourteen kilometres) west of Thurso.
why_interesting: The site of Britain's pioneering nuclear research establishment.

name: Dunbeath Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Dunbeath Castle is located on the east coast of Caithness, 2 kilometres (1.2 mi) south of Dunbeath, in northern Scotland. Although a castle has stood here since the 15th century, the present building is of mainly 17th-century origin, with 19th-century extensions.
why_interesting: A dramatic clifftop castle overlooking the North Sea.

name: Dunrobin Castle
why_interesting: One of Scotland's grandest fairytale castles, inspired by French châteaux.

name: Inverness Castle
why_interesting: The landmark castle overlooking the River Ness in the heart of Inverness.

name: Kinlochaline Castle
why_interesting: A beautifully restored 16th-century tower house hidden in Morvern.

name: Skibo Castle
why_interesting: A luxurious Highland estate hidden among ancient woodland.

name: Auchindoun Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Auchindoun Castle is a 15th-century L-Plan tower castle located in Auchindoun near Dufftown in Moray, Scotland.
why_interesting: The impressive ruins of a medieval fortress overlooking Strathspey.

name: Balvenie Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Balvenie Castle is a ruined castle 1 km north of Dufftown in the Moray region of Scotland.
why_interesting: The magnificent ruins of one of Scotland's greatest medieval castles.

name: Gordon Castle
why_interesting: A grand country house standing on the historic Gordon family estate.

name: Hawthornden Castle
why_interesting: The romantic riverside retreat of poet William Drummond.

name: Melville Castle
why_interesting: A magnificent baronial mansion just south of Edinburgh.

name: Balvaird Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Balvaird Castle in Perthshire is a traditional late medieval Scottish tower house. It is located in the Ochil Hills, around five kilometres (three miles) south of Abernethy.
why_interesting: A remarkably intact Z-plan tower house overlooking rural Perthshire.

name: Bishop's Palace, Kirkwall
Wikipedia Extract: The Bishop's Palace, Kirkwall is a 12th-century palace built at the same time as the adjacent St Magnus Cathedral in the centre of Kirkwall, Orkney, Scotland. It housed the cathedral's first bishop, William the Old of the Norwegian Catholic Church who took his authority from the Archbishop of Nidaros (Trondheim).
why_interesting: The beautifully preserved medieval palace beside St Magnus Cathedral.

name: Lochranza Castle
why_interesting: The picturesque ruins of a medieval castle overlooking Loch Ranza.

name: Portencross Castle
why_interesting: One of Scotland's best-preserved medieval tower houses overlooking the Firth of Clyde.

name: Blair Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Blair Castle (in Scottish Gaelic: Caisteil Bhlàir) stands in its grounds near the village of Blair Atholl in Perthshire in Scotland. It is the ancestral home of the Clan Murray, and was historically the seat of their chief, the Duke of Atholl, though the current chief, the 12th Duke of Atholl, lives in South Africa, where he was born and raised.
why_interesting: The magnificent ancestral home of the Dukes of Atholl, surrounded by Highland scenery and centuries of clan history.

name: Burleigh Castle
Wikipedia Extract: The remains of Burleigh Castle are located just outside the village of Milnathort, 1.5 miles north of Kinross, in Perth and Kinross, Scotland. The castle dates from the 15th and 16th centuries, and now sits beside the A911 road, opposite a 19th-century steading, recently adapted into housing.
why_interesting: One of Scotland's oldest tower houses, overlooking the Ochil Hills.

name: Castle Menzies
Wikipedia Extract: Castle Menzies in Scotland is the ancestral seat of the Clan Menzies and the Menzies Baronets. It is located a little to the west of the small village of Weem, near Aberfeldy in the Highlands of Perthshire, close to the former site of Weem Castle, destroyed c.
why_interesting: A beautifully restored 16th-century castle overlooking the Tay Valley.

name: Drummond Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Drummond Castle is located in Perthshire, Scotland. The castle is known for its gardens, described by Historic Environment Scotland as "the best example of formal terraced gardens in Scotland." It is situated in Muthill parish, 4 kilometres (2.5 mi) south of Crieff.
why_interesting: A spectacular Renaissance castle renowned for its magnificent terraced gardens.

name: Elcho Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Elcho Castle () is located close to the south bank of the River Tay approximately four miles south-east of Perth, Scotland, in the region of Perth and Kinross. It was maintained by Clan Wemyss from its construction around 1560 until it was put into the care of the Secretary of State for Scotland in the early 20th century, though was not occupied for the entire time.
why_interesting: One of Scotland's best-preserved Renaissance tower houses overlooking the River Tay.

name: Huntingtower Castle
why_interesting: A rare twin-towered castle with one of Scotland's most unusual medieval designs.

name: Methven Castle
why_interesting: The historic seat of the Murrays of Methven, rebuilt as an elegant country house.

name: Berwick Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Berwick Castle is a ruined castle in Berwick-upon-Tweed, Northumberland, England.
why_interesting: The earthwork remains of Berwick's mighty medieval fortress overlooking the Tweed.

name: Branxholme Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Branxholme Castle is a five-storey tower at Branxholme, about 3 miles south-west of Hawick in the Borders region of Scotland.
why_interesting: A magnificent Borders castle that has been home to the Dukes of Buccleuch for centuries.

name: Cessford Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Cessford Castle, is a large ruined mid-15th century L-plan castle near the village of Cessford, midway Jedburgh and Kelso, in the historic county of Roxburghshire, now a division of the Scottish Borders. The Castle is caput of the Barony of Cessford, and the principal stronghold of the Kerr family, notorious Border Reivers, many of whom served as Wardens of the Middle March.
why_interesting: The imposing ruins of one of the Borders' strongest medieval fortresses.

name: Duns Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Duns Castle, Duns, Berwickshire is a historic house in Scotland, the oldest part of which, the massive Norman Keep or Pele Tower, supposedly dates from 1320. The castle and most of the structures on the property are designated as a Category A listed building.
why_interesting: A grand Gothic Revival mansion set within beautiful parkland.

name: Ferniehirst Castle
why_interesting: A beautifully restored Borders tower house overlooking the Jed Water.

name: Floors Castle
why_interesting: Scotland's largest inhabited castle, surrounded by magnificent gardens on the River Tweed.

name: Hermitage Castle
why_interesting: One of Scotland's most haunting medieval fortresses, isolated in the Borders.

name: Neidpath Castle
why_interesting: A romantic medieval castle overlooking the River Tweed.

name: Blairquhan Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Blairquhan ( blair-WHAHN, Scots: Blairwhan) is a Regency era castle near Maybole in South Ayrshire, Scotland. It was the historic home of the Hunter-Blair Baronets and remained in the family's possession until 2012, when it was sold to the bottled water company Ganten.
why_interesting: A magnificent Victorian baronial mansion in the Ayrshire countryside.

name: Bothwell Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Bothwell Castle is a large medieval castle, sited on a high, steep bank, above a bend in  the River Clyde in South Lanarkshire, Scotland. It is located between Bothwell and Uddingston, about 10 miles (16 km) south-east of Glasgow.
why_interesting: One of Scotland's finest Norman castles, dramatically overlooking the River Clyde.

name: Craignethan Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Craignethan Castle is a ruined castle in South Lanarkshire, Scotland. It is located above the River Nethan, a tributary of the River Clyde, at NS816464.
why_interesting: A spectacular Renaissance fortress with some of Scotland's finest surviving gun loops.

name: Culzean Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Culzean Castle ( kul-AYN, see yogh; Scots: Culzean, Culȝean, Colean) is a castle overlooking the Firth of Clyde, near Maybole, Carrick, in South Ayrshire, on the west coast of Scotland. It is the former home of the Marquess of Ailsa, the chief of Clan Kennedy, but is now owned by the National Trust for Scotland.
why_interesting: One of Scotland's grandest clifftop castles, perched above the Firth of Clyde.

name: Dunure Castle
why_interesting: The picturesque ruins of a medieval fortress overlooking the Ayrshire coast.

name: Muness Castle
why_interesting: Shetland's best-preserved laird's castle, standing at Britain's northernmost inhabited settlement.

name: Scalloway Castle
why_interesting: The impressive ruins of Shetland's former Earl's palace.

name: Thirlestane Castle
why_interesting: A magnificent 16th-century castle surrounded by landscaped grounds.

name: Balloch Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Balloch Castle is an early 19th-century country house situated at the southern tip of Loch Lomond, in West Dunbartonshire, Scotland. Balloch was a property of the Lennox family from the 11th century, and the old castle was built in the 13th century.
why_interesting: A picturesque country park centred around a grand 19th-century castle.

name: Culcreuch Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Culcreuch Castle is a Scottish castle close to the village of Fintry, near Loch Lomond. It had been the home of the Barons of Culcreuch since 1699.
why_interesting: A charming castle hotel hidden within the Campsie Fells.

name: Doune Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Doune Castle is a medieval stronghold near the village of Doune, in the Stirling council area of central Scotland and the historic county of Perthshire.  The castle is sited on a wooded bend where the Ardoch Burn flows into the River Teith.
why_interesting: One of Scotland's best-preserved medieval castles, featured in *Monty Python* and *Outlander*.

name: Dumbarton Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Dumbarton Castle (Scottish Gaelic: Dùn Breatainn, pronounced [t̪unˈpɾʲɛʰt̪ɪɲ]; Welsh: Alt Clut) has the longest recorded history of any stronghold in Scotland. It sits on a volcanic plug of basalt known as Dumbarton Rock which is 240 feet (73 m) high and overlooks the Scottish town of Dumbarton.
why_interesting: A dramatic fortress perched atop volcanic rock overlooking the River Clyde.

name: Edinample Castle
why_interesting: A picturesque Highland tower house overlooking Loch Earn.

name: Stirling Castle
why_interesting: Scotland's most iconic royal fortress, dominating the skyline of Stirling.

name: Strathaven Castle
why_interesting: The impressive ruins of a medieval royal castle overlooking Strathaven.

name: Armadale Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Armadale Castle is a ruined country house in Armadale, Skye, former home of the MacDonalds.
why_interesting: The romantic gardens and ruined castle of Clan Donald on the Isle of Skye.

name: Crawford Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Crawford Castle, substantially in ruins, is located on the north bank of the River Clyde, around 1⁄2 mile (800 metres) north of Crawford, South Lanarkshire, Scotland. The ruins stand on an earlier motte and bailey earthwork.
why_interesting: The atmospheric remains of one of Scotland's oldest royal castles.

name: Dunimarle Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Dunimarle Castle is located 1 km west of the centre of the village of Culross in Fife, Scotland. The name 'Dunimarle' means 'castle by the sea', although the original name of the estate was 'Castlehill'.
why_interesting: A handsome Victorian mansion overlooking the Firth of Forth.

name: Dunvegan Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Dunvegan Castle (Caisteal Dhùn Bheagain) is located 1 mile (1.6 km) to the north of Dunvegan on the Isle of Skye, off the west coast of Scotland. It is the seat of the MacLeod of MacLeod, chief of the Clan MacLeod.
why_interesting: The oldest continuously inhabited castle in Scotland, home to Clan MacLeod for 800 years.

name: Redcastle
why_interesting: A picturesque medieval tower house overlooking the Beauly Firth.

name: Smailholm Tower
why_interesting: One of Scotland's most iconic tower houses, standing alone above the Borders countryside.

name: Aros Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Aros Castle, also known as Dounarwyse Castle, is a ruined 13th-century castle near Salen on the Isle of Mull, Scotland. The castle overlooks the Sound of Mull.
why_interesting: The ruins of a medieval castle overlooking the Sound of Mull.

name: Auldhame Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Auldhame Castle is a ruined L-plan tower house standing on a ridge above Seacliff beach, about 3 miles east of North Berwick in East Lothian, and less than half a mile from Tantallon Castle.
why_interesting: The dramatic clifftop ruins of a medieval East Lothian tower house.

name: Balquhain Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Balquhain Castle is a ruined tower house in Aberdeenshire, Scotland. It served as the stronghold of the Leslies of Balquhain.
why_interesting: The romantic ruins of a powerful Gordon family stronghold.

name: Drumcoltran Tower
Wikipedia Extract:
Drumcoltran Tower is a late-16th-century tower house situated in the historical county of Kirkcudbrightshire  near Kirkgunzeon, Dumfries and Galloway.
Like other towers in the area, Drumcoltran was built by a branch of the Maxwell family around 1570 but passed with the estate to the Irvings in 1668.
why_interesting: A well-preserved Scottish tower house overlooking the Solway countryside.

name: Dundonald Castle, Kintyre
Wikipedia Extract: Dundonald Castle is a ruined castle near Killean, Kintyre, Scotland. It was a stronghold of Clan Donald, but later passed to the Campbells.
why_interesting: The ruins of a medieval castle overlooking Campbeltown Loch.

name: Eden Castle
Wikipedia Extract:
Eden Castle is a castle near Banff in Aberdeenshire, Scotland.
The castle was built in the latter half of the 16th century by the Meldrum family with renovation and additional building carried out by George Leslie from 1676.
why_interesting: A handsome Victorian mansion surrounded by mature woodland.

name: Knockhall Castle
why_interesting: The picturesque ruins of a medieval tower overlooking Stonehaven Bay.

name: Beaumaris Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Beaumaris Castle ( bew-MAR-is; Welsh: Castell Biwmares, Welsh pronunciation: [kastɛɬ bɪuˈmaːrɛs]), in Beaumaris, Anglesey, Wales, was built as part of Edward I's campaign to conquer north Wales after 1282. Plans were probably first made to construct the castle in 1284, but this was delayed due to lack of funds and work only began in 1295 following the Madog ap Llywelyn uprising.
why_interesting: Edward I's perfectly symmetrical masterpiece overlooking the Menai Strait.

name: Caerphilly Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Caerphilly Castle (Welsh: Castell Caerffili) is a medieval fortification in Caerphilly in South Wales. The castle was constructed by Gilbert de Clare in the 13th century as part of his campaign to maintain control of Glamorgan, and saw extensive fighting between Gilbert, his descendants, and the native Welsh rulers.
why_interesting: One of the largest medieval castles in Europe, surrounded by water-filled defences.

name: Cardiff Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Cardiff Castle (Welsh: Castell Caerdydd) is a medieval castle and Victorian Gothic revival mansion located in the city centre of Cardiff, Wales. The original motte and bailey castle was built in the late 11th century by Norman invaders on top of a 3rd-century Roman fort.
why_interesting: A spectacular fortress blending Roman walls, Norman keeps and lavish Victorian interiors.

name: Carew Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Carew Castle (Welsh: Castell Caeriw) is a castle in the civil parish of Carew in Pembrokeshire, Wales. The Carew family take their name from this site and have owned the castle for more than 900 years.
why_interesting: One of Wales' finest tidal castles, beautifully reflected in its surrounding millpond.

name: Castell Coch
Wikipedia Extract: Castell Coch (Welsh for 'red castle'; Welsh pronunciation: [ˈkas.tɛɬ koːχ]) is a 19th-century Gothic Revival castle built above the village of Tongwynlais in Wales. The first castle on the site was built by the Normans after 1081 to protect the newly conquered town of Cardiff and control the route along the River Taff.
why_interesting: A fairy-tale Gothic Revival castle hidden within ancient woodland.

name: Conwy Castle
why_interesting: One of Europe's best-preserved medieval walled castles overlooking the Conwy Estuary.

name: Candleston Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Candleston Castle (historically sometimes Candlestone Castle) is a 14th-century fortified manor house, in ruins since the 19th century. It is 0.75 miles (1.2 km) southwest of Merthyr Mawr, Glamorgan, Wales, now Bridgend County Borough and just 0.75 miles (1.2 km) northwest of Ogmore Castle, separated by the River Ogmore.
why_interesting: The romantic ruins of a Norman manor hidden within Merthyr Mawr sand dunes.

name: Chepstow Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Chepstow Castle (Welsh: Castell Cas-gwent) at Chepstow, Monmouthshire, Wales, is the oldest surviving post-Roman stone fortification in Britain.  Located above cliffs on the River Wye, construction began in 1067 under the instruction of the Norman Lord William FitzOsbern.
why_interesting: Britain's oldest surviving stone castle, dramatically overlooking the River Wye.

name: Oystermouth Castle
why_interesting: A beautifully restored Norman castle overlooking Swansea Bay.

name: Powis Castle
why_interesting: A magnificent medieval fortress famed for its world-class gardens and art collection.

name: Swansea Castle
why_interesting: The impressive riverside ruins of Swansea's Norman castle.

name: Aberdyfi Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Aberdyfi Castle is a castle located near Glandyfi, Ceredigion, in Wales. All that now remains is the motte, which is referred to as Domen Las (traditionally meaning "blue mound" in Welsh).
why_interesting: The earthwork remains of a Norman fortress overlooking the Dyfi Estuary.

name: Castell Dinas Brân
Wikipedia Extract: Castell Dinas Brân is a medieval castle, built by the Princes of Powys Fadog, which occupies a prominent hilltop site above the town of Llangollen in Denbighshire, Wales. The presently visible stone castle was probably built in the 1260s by Gruffydd Maelor II, a prince of Powys Fadog, on the site of several earlier structures, including an Iron Age hillfort.
why_interesting: The spectacular hilltop ruins of Wales' legendary 'Crow Castle'.

name: Castell y Bere
Wikipedia Extract: Castell y Bere is a Welsh castle near Llanfihangel-y-pennant in Gwynedd, Wales. Constructed by Llywelyn the Great in the 1220s, the stone castle was intended to maintain his authority over the local people and to defend the south-west part of the princedom of Gwynedd.
why_interesting: The dramatic ruins of Llywelyn the Great's mountain stronghold.

name: Dinas Emrys
Wikipedia Extract: Dinas Emrys (Welsh for 'Emrys's city') is a rocky and wooded hillock near Beddgelert in Gwynedd, north-west Wales. Rising some 76 m (250 ft) above the floor of the Glaslyn river valley, it overlooks the southern end of Llyn Dinas in Snowdonia.
why_interesting: The legendary hill fort linked to Merlin and the tales of King Arthur.

name: Dinerth Castle
Wikipedia Extract: The Castle of Dinerth (Welsh: Castell Dineirth, Castell Dinerth, or Castell Allt Craig Arth) is a Welsh castle located near Aberarth, Ceredigion, west Wales that was completed c. AD 1110. It is also known as Hero Castle, presumably from the Norse hiro ("king's carl").
why_interesting: The earthwork remains of a Norman castle overlooking Cardigan Bay.

name: Dolbadarn Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Dolbadarn Castle (English:  dol-BAD-an; Welsh: Castell Dolbadarn; Welsh pronunciation: [kastɛɬ dɔl'badarn]) is a fortification built by the Welsh prince Llywelyn the Great during the early 13th century, at the base of the Llanberis Pass, in northern Wales. The castle was important both militarily and as a symbol of Llywelyn's power and authority.
why_interesting: One of Wales' most iconic native castles beneath the mountains of Eryri.

name: Dolforwyn Castle
why_interesting: The impressive hilltop ruins of Llywelyn ap Gruffudd's final great fortress.

name: Aberedw Castle
Wikipedia Extract: The remains of Aberedw Castle, also known as 'Castle in Elfael Uwch Mynydd', are located at the small village of Aberedw in the county of Powys, Mid-Wales. It was built in the late twelfth century and probably replaced the motte and bailey castle a few hundred metres away.
why_interesting: The peaceful riverside ruins of a Norman border castle.

name: Bronllys
Wikipedia Extract: Bronllys is a village and community situated in Powys, Wales, nestled between the towns of Brecon and Talgarth. The village is part of the historic county of Brecknockshire (Breconshire) and serves as an electoral ward for Powys County Council.
why_interesting: The remarkably preserved motte-and-bailey overlooking the Usk Valley.

name: Chirk Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Chirk Castle (Welsh: Castell y Waun) is a Grade I listed castle located in Chirk, Wrexham County Borough, Wales,  1.5 mi (2.4 km) from Chirk railway station, now owned and run by the National Trust.
why_interesting: A magnificent medieval fortress that has remained a family home for more than 700 years.

name: Cresswell Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Cresswell Castle is a castle half a mile north of the village of Cresswell Quay, Pembrokeshire, west Wales. It is situated on the banks of the River Cresswell in what is currently private land.
why_interesting: The earthwork remains of a Norman castle overlooking the Pembrokeshire countryside.

name: Loughor Castle
why_interesting: The picturesque riverside ruins of a Norman castle overlooking the Loughor Estuary.

name: Penrice Castle
why_interesting: A grand country estate centred around a medieval castle on the Gower Peninsula.

name: Picton Castle
why_interesting: A magnificent Pembrokeshire castle still serving as a family home.

name: Audley's Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Audley's Castle is a 15th-century castle located 1 mile (1.6 km) north-east of Strangford, County Down, Northern Ireland, on a rocky height overlooking Strangford Lough. It is a three-storey Tower house named after its 16th century owner, John Audley.
why_interesting: A picturesque tower house overlooking Strangford Lough.

name: Bangor Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Bangor Castle is a country house situated in Castle Park in Bangor, County Down, Northern Ireland. The building, which is also referred to as Bangor City Hall and is now used as the offices of Ards and North Down Borough Council, is a Grade A listed building.
why_interesting: A handsome Victorian castle overlooking Bangor Marina.

name: Belfast Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Belfast Castle (Irish: Caisleán Bhéal Feirste) is a mansion located in Cave Hill Country Park in Belfast, Northern Ireland, in a prominent position 400 feet (120 m) above sea level. Its location provides unobstructed views over the City of Belfast and Belfast Lough.
why_interesting: A magnificent Scottish Baronial mansion overlooking Belfast Lough.

name: Carrickfergus Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Carrickfergus Castle (from the Irish Carraig Ḟergus or "cairn of Fergus", the name "Fergus" meaning "strong man") is a Norman castle in Northern Ireland, situated in the town of Carrickfergus in County Antrim, on the northern shore of Belfast Lough. Besieged in turn by the Scottish, rebel Irish, English, and French, the castle played an important military role until 1928 and remains one of the best preserved medieval structures in Northern Ireland.
why_interesting: One of Ireland's finest Norman castles, standing proudly above Belfast Lough.

name: Dunluce Castle
why_interesting: One of Ireland's most spectacular cliff-top castle ruins overlooking the Atlantic.

name: Hillsborough Castle
why_interesting: The official residence of the Secretary of State for Northern Ireland, surrounded by beautiful gardens.

name: Kilclief Castle
why_interesting: One of Ireland's best-preserved tower houses overlooking Strangford Lough.

name: Narrow Water Castle
why_interesting: A picturesque Gothic Revival mansion overlooking the Newry River.

name: Olderfleet Castle
why_interesting: A remarkably preserved Scottish tower house guarding Larne Harbour.

name: Benburb Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Benburb Castle is a castle situated in Benburb, County Tyrone, Northern Ireland.  It is built on a limestone cliff overlooking the River Blackwater, the border between County Tyrone and County Armagh.
why_interesting: The dramatic ruins of a plantation-era castle overlooking the River Blackwater.

name: Castle Balfour
Wikipedia Extract: Castle Balfour is a castle situated in Lisnaskea, County Fermanagh, Northern Ireland. It sits at the edge of the parish graveyard just west of Main Street.
why_interesting: A magnificent Scottish Baronial mansion overlooking the shores of Lough Erne.

name: Harry Avery's Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Harry Avery's Castle is situated half a mile south-west of Newtownstewart, in County Tyrone, Northern Ireland. It is a rare example of a stone castle built by a Gaelic Irish chief, although its origins and history are uncertain.
why_interesting: The remote ruins of a medieval hilltop fortress overlooking the Sperrin Mountains.

name: Killymoon Castle
Wikipedia Extract:
Killymoon Castle is a castle situated about one mile (1.6 km) south east of Cookstown, County Tyrone, Northern Ireland, on the north bank of the Ballinderry River. 
It is located above the Ballinderry River with a back-drop of woodland and parkland.
why_interesting: A magnificent Gothic Revival castle overlooking the River Blackwater in County Tyrone.

name: Monea castle
Wikipedia Extract: Monea Castle is a castle located  in Monea, County Fermanagh, Northern Ireland. It is a State Care Historic Monument situated in the townland of Castletown Monea, in Fermanagh District Council area, at grid ref: H1647 4937.
why_interesting: One of Ireland's finest surviving plantation castles overlooking Lower Lough Erne.

name: Mountjoy Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Mountjoy Castle is a ruined fortification situated near the village of Brockagh, in Magheralamfield townland in County Tyrone, Northern Ireland, on a hill overlooking Lough Neagh. The castle played a role in the Irish Rebellion of 1641 when it was captured by the forces of  Felim O'Neill of Kinard under the command of Turlough Gruama O'Quinn.
why_interesting: The ruined plantation fortress built by Lord Mountjoy during the Nine Years' War.

name: Necarne
Wikipedia Extract:
Necarne Castle, also known as Castle Irvine, is a Victorian gothic house near Irvinestown in County Fermanagh, Northern Ireland.
The two-storey façade was designed by John Benjamin Keane and was completed in 1835.
why_interesting: A grand Victorian Gothic mansion surrounded by one of Fermanagh's finest estates.

name: Tully Castle
why_interesting: One of Ulster's best-preserved plantation castles overlooking Lough Erne.

name: Barryscourt Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Barryscourt Castle (Caisleán Chúirt an Bharraigh in Irish) is a castle located in eastern County Cork in southern Ireland, close to the town of Carrigtwohill.
why_interesting: One of Ireland's finest restored tower houses, complete with impressive defensive features.

name: Belvelly Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Belvelly Castle is a 14th or 15th-century tower house in County Cork, Ireland. It is situated next to the small village of Belvelly, opposite and overlooking the only road bridge connecting Fota Island to Great Island (on which the town of Cobh is situated).
why_interesting: A striking medieval tower house guarding the entrance to Great Island.

name: Blackwater Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Blackwater Castle, also and formerly known as Castle Widenham, is a privately owned estate located in the village of Castletownroche between the towns of Mallow and Fermoy in north County Cork, Ireland. Since 2005 it has been available to rent as a private hire venue for castle weddings and private parties along with castle rentals for vacations.
why_interesting: A romantic riverside castle overlooking the Blackwater Valley.

name: Blarney Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Blarney Castle (Irish: Caisleán na Blarnan) is a medieval stronghold in Blarney, a town in Cork, Ireland. Though earlier fortifications were built on the same spot, the current keep was built by the MacCarthy of Muskerry dynasty, a cadet branch of the Kings of Desmond, and dates from 1446.
why_interesting: Home to the legendary Blarney Stone, kissed by visitors for over 500 years.

name: Bunratty Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Bunratty Castle (Irish: Caisleán Bhun Raithe) is a large 15th-century tower house in County Clare, Ireland. It is located in the centre of Bunratty village, by the N18 road between Limerick and Ennis, near Shannon Town and its airport.
why_interesting: Ireland's most complete medieval tower house, brought vividly to life with period interiors.

name: Doonagore Castle
why_interesting: A picturesque tower house perched dramatically above the Cliffs of Moher.

name: Leamaneh Castle
why_interesting: The atmospheric ruins of a fortified tower house and grand manor in the Burren.

name: O'Dea Castle
why_interesting: A beautifully restored tower house showcasing the history of the O'Dea clan.

name: Ballymore Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Ballymore Castle in Lawrencetown, County Galway, Ireland was originally a 15th-century tower house belonging to O'Madden. A house was added in 1620, and the castle has been much altered since then.
why_interesting: A well-preserved Norman tower house hidden in the Galway countryside.

name: Carrickmines Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Carrickmines Castle is an archaeological site in Carrickmines, County Dublin, in eastern Ireland. The castle was built in the Middle Ages to protect the English-ruled Pale around Dublin.
why_interesting: The impressive ruins of one of Dublin's largest Norman castles.

name: Doe Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Doe Castle, or Caisleán na dTuath, near Creeslough, County Donegal, was the historical stronghold of Clan tSuibhne (Clan McSweeney), with architectural parallels to the Scottish tower house. Built in the early 15th century, it is one of the better fortalices in the north-west of Ireland.
why_interesting: A beautifully preserved waterside fortress overlooking Sheephaven Bay.

name: Donegal Castle
why_interesting: The restored stronghold of the O'Donnell clan at the heart of Donegal Town.

name: Dunboy Castle
why_interesting: The dramatic ruins of an important O'Sullivan stronghold overlooking Bantry Bay.

name: Glenveagh Castle
why_interesting: A spectacular Scottish-style castle surrounded by the wild beauty of Glenveagh National Park.

name: Liscarroll Castle
why_interesting: One of Ireland's largest surviving medieval castles, with massive curtain walls.

name: Ballycarbery Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Ballycarbery Castle is a castle 3 kilometres (2 mi) from Cahersiveen, County Kerry, Ireland. The castle is high on a grass hill facing the sea and is a short distance from Cahergall Fort and Leacanabuile Fort.
why_interesting: The ivy-clad ruins of one of Kerry's most photographed castles.

name: Dromore Castle (County Kerry)
Wikipedia Extract: Dromore Castle is a manor house in Templenoe, County Kerry, Ireland, looking out over the Kenmare River. It was built in the 1830s for the Mahony family to a neo-Gothic design by Sir Thomas Deane.
why_interesting: The romantic ruins of a Victorian Gothic mansion overlooking Killarney National Park.

name: Dunguaire Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Dunguaire Castle (Irish: Dún Guaire) is a 16th-century tower house on the southeastern shore of Galway Bay in County Galway, Ireland, near Kinvara (also spelled Kinvarra). The name derives from the dun (fort) of King Guaire, the legendary king of Connacht.
why_interesting: One of Ireland's most iconic tower houses, standing proudly on Galway Bay.

name: Eyrecourt Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Eyrecourt Castle (or Eyre Court) was an Irish 17th century country house in Galway which became a ruin in the 20th century. The house, the surrounding estate, and the nearby small town of Eyrecourt all took their name from Colonel the Right Hon.
why_interesting: The romantic ruins of a once-grand Georgian mansion in east Galway.

name: Gallarus Castle
why_interesting: A remarkably preserved tower house overlooking the Dingle Peninsula.

name: Listowel Castle
why_interesting: The impressive riverside fortress dominating the centre of Listowel.

name: Maynooth Castle
why_interesting: The magnificent ruins of the Fitzgerald family's principal stronghold.

name: Parkavonear Castle
why_interesting: A secluded medieval tower house overlooking Killarney's lakes.

name: Ross Castle

name: Ballaghmore, County Laois
Wikipedia Extract: Ballaghmore (historically Bellaghmore, from Irish: an Bealach Mór, meaning 'the great way') is a small village located on the western side of County Laois, Ireland, southwest of Portlaoise. It is approximately 7 kilometres (4 mi) east of Roscrea.
why_interesting: A remarkably preserved tower house overlooking the Laois countryside.

name: Carrigogunnell
Wikipedia Extract:
Carrigogunnell Castle (Irish: Chairrge Ó gCoinneall) is a medieval Irish fortification near the village of Clarina, on the banks of the River Shannon in County Limerick.
The structure dates to at least the early 13th century, and was slighted in September 1691 after being captured during the second siege of Limerick.
why_interesting: The dramatic riverside ruins of one of Limerick's finest Norman castles.

name: Castle Oliver
Wikipedia Extract: Castle Oliver (also Clonodfoy) is a Victorian castle-style country house in the southern part of County Limerick, Ireland. Built for entertaining rather than for defense, it has a ballroom, drawing room, library, morning room, dining room and hall which feature hand-painted ceilings, decorated ornamental corbels, superbly executed stained glass windows and stencil work.
why_interesting: One of Ireland's grandest Gothic Revival castles, built on a truly palatial scale.

name: Dunamase
Wikipedia Extract: Dunamase or the Rock of Dunamase (Irish: Dún Másc "fort of Másc") is a rocky outcrop in County Laois, Ireland. Rising 46 metres (151 ft) above a plain, it has the ruins of Dunamase Castle, a defensive stronghold dating from the early Hiberno-Norman period with a view across to the Slieve Bloom Mountains.
why_interesting: One of Ireland's most spectacular hilltop fortresses with panoramic Midlands views.

name: Foulksrath Castle
why_interesting: A beautifully restored medieval tower house operating as a unique castle hotel.

name: Kilkenny Castle
why_interesting: The magnificent Norman castle at the heart of Kilkenny City.

name: Purt Castle
why_interesting: A medieval tower house overlooking the Shannon Estuary.

name: Ashford Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Ashford Castle is a mainly Victorian and medieval castle near Cong on the County Mayo–Galway border in Ireland. The castle has been expanded over the centuries and turned into a five star hotel.
why_interesting: One of Ireland's finest castle hotels, surrounded by woodland and overlooking Lough Corrib.

name: Birr Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Birr Castle (Irish: Caisleán Bhiorra) is a castle in the town of Birr in County Offaly, Ireland. It is the home of the 7th Earl of Rosse and his family, and as such the castle is generally not open to the public, though the grounds and gardens of the demesne are publicly accessible, and include a science museum and a café, a reflecting telescope which was the largest in the world for decades and a modern radio telescope.
why_interesting: Home to the world-famous Leviathan telescope and spectacular formal gardens.

name: Charleville Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Charleville Castle is a Gothic-style castle located in County Offaly, Ireland, bordering the town of Tullamore, near the River Clodiagh.  It is considered one of the finest of its type in the country.

name: Eboracum
Wikipedia Extract: Eboracum (Classical Latin: [ɛbɔˈraːkũː]) was a fort and later a city in the Roman province of Britannia. In its prime it was the largest town in northern Britannia and a provincial capital.
why_interesting: The Roman fortress that became the foundation of the city of York.

name: Ham Hill, Somerset
Wikipedia Extract:
Ham Hill is a geological Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI), Scheduled Ancient Monument, Iron Age hill fort, Roman site, Local Nature Reserve and country park, to the west of Yeovil in Somerset, England.
The hill has given its name to the distinctive quarried hamstone and also to two nearby villages: Stoke-sub-Hamdon and Norton Sub Hamdon, whose names mean "under-Ham-hill" (where "Ham" is Old English for a small settlement).
why_interesting: One of Britain's largest Iron Age hillforts, with sweeping views across Somerset.

name: Admiralty Pier Turret
Wikipedia Extract: The Admiralty Pier Turret, or Dover Turret, is an enclosed armoured turret built in 1882 on the western breakwater of Dover Harbour in southeast England. It contains two Fraser RML 16 inch 80 ton guns, the biggest installed in the United Kingdom.
why_interesting: A Victorian gun turret guarding the entrance to Dover Harbour.

name: Cawsand
Wikipedia Extract: Cawsand (Cornish: Porthbugh; lit. Cow Cove) and Kingsand (Cornish: Porthruw) are twin villages in southeast Cornwall, England, United Kingdom.
why_interesting: The remains of coastal fortifications overlooking Plymouth Sound.

name: Dover Western Heights
Wikipedia Extract: The Western Heights of Dover is a series of forts and ditches in Dover, England. They were created in the 18th and 19th centuries to augment the existing defences and protect the key port of Dover from both seaward and landward attack.
why_interesting: An immense Victorian fortress defending Dover from attack.

name: Fort Burgoyne
Wikipedia Extract: Fort Burgoyne, originally known as Castle Hill Fort, was built in the 1860s as one of the Palmerston forts around Dover in southeast England. It was built to a polygonal system with detached eastern and western redoubts, to guard the high ground northeast of the strategic port of Dover, just north of Dover Castle.
why_interesting: One of Britain's largest Napoleonic hill forts overlooking the English Channel.

name: Hougham Battery
Wikipedia Extract:
Hougham Battery is a World War II coastal defence battery built in 1941 between Dover and Folkestone in southeast England.
It is on the cliff-edge between Abbot's Cliff and Shakespeare Cliff.
why_interesting: The remains of a Victorian coastal battery overlooking the Strait of Dover.

name: Fort Albert
Wikipedia Extract: Fort Albert (map reference SZ330890) is a tower fort nestling under the cliffs south-west of Fort Victoria on the Isle of Wight, England. It was also known as Cliff End Fort, named after the Northern extremity of Colwell Bay (Cliff's End).
why_interesting: A Victorian Palmerston fort guarding the western Solent.

name: Fort Blockhouse
Wikipedia Extract: Fort Blockhouse is a former military establishment in Gosport, Hampshire, England, and the final version of a complicated site. At its greatest extent in the 19th century, the structure was part of a set of fortifications which encircled much of Gosport.
why_interesting: One of Britain's oldest continuously occupied military fortifications overlooking Portsmouth Harbour.

name: Fortifications of Portsmouth
Wikipedia Extract: The fortifications of Portsmouth are extensive due to its strategic position on the English Channel and role as home to the Royal Navy. For this reason, Portsmouth was, by the 19th century, one of the most fortified cities in the world.
why_interesting: The vast network of walls and bastions that once made Portsmouth Britain's premier fortress city.

name: Crownhill Fort
Wikipedia Extract: Crownhill Fort is a Royal Commission Fort built in the 1860s in Crownhill as part of Lord Palmerston's ring of land defences for Plymouth. Restored by the Landmark Trust, it is now home to several small businesses, museums, exhibitions and a holiday apartment sleeping up to eight people.
why_interesting: One of Britain's best-preserved Victorian forts, packed with original artillery and tunnels.

name: Fort Amherst
Wikipedia Extract: Fort Amherst is a Napoleonic-era military fortress in Chatham, Kent, England. It was constructed between April and October 1756 at the southern end of the Brompton Lines during the Seven Years’ War, with the primary purpose of defending Chatham Dockyard and the River Medway from a potential French invasion.
why_interesting: A spectacular Napoleonic fortress overlooking the Medway.

name: Fort Borstal
Wikipedia Extract: Fort Borstal was built as an afterthought from the 1859 Royal Commission on the Defence of the United Kingdom, by convict labour. Construction started in 1875 but was suspended in 1885.
why_interesting: A Victorian hill fort overlooking Rochester and the Medway towns.

name: Fort Cumberland (England)
Wikipedia Extract: Fort Cumberland is a pentagonal artillery fortification erected to guard the entrance to Langstone Harbour, east of the Dockyard of Portsmouth on the south coast of England. It was sited to protect the Royal Navy Dockyard, by preventing enemy forces from landing in Langstone Harbour and attacking from the landward side.
why_interesting: A star-shaped artillery fort protecting the eastern approaches to Portsmouth.

name: Fort Darnet
Wikipedia Extract: Fort Darnet is a nineteenth-century military installation on the River Medway in Kent, England, that formed part of the defences of Chatham Naval Dockyard. Fort Darnet, like its twin Hoo Fort 1 km (0.6 mi) upstream, was built on the recommendations of the 1859 Royal Commission on an island covering Pinup Reach, the inner navigable channel of the River Medway.
why_interesting: A lonely island fort guarding the Medway Estuary.

name: Fort Luton
Wikipedia Extract:
Fort Luton was built between 1876 and 1892 south of Chatham, Medway, South East England.
It is one of the five late Victorian land front forts built to defend the overland approaches to Chatham.
why_interesting: A Victorian fort built to defend Chatham Dockyard.

name: Brackenbury Battery
Wikipedia Extract: Brackenbury Battery was a small coastal artillery fort located just north of Felixstowe, England, and initially known as Felixstowe Battery. It opened in October 1915 to provide fire northward from the Haven ports, replacing a battery of 10-inch guns that had previously covered this area.
why_interesting: The remains of a Victorian coastal battery overlooking Harwich Harbour.

name: Brean Down Fort
Wikipedia Extract: Brean Down Fort was a Victorian naval fortification designed to protect the Bristol Channel. It was built 60 feet (18 m) above sea level on the headland at Brean Down, 9 miles (14 km) south of Weston-super-Mare, Somerset, England.
why_interesting: A dramatic Victorian fort perched on the cliffs above the Bristol Channel.

name: Fort Paull
Wikipedia Extract: Fort Paull is a gun battery situated on the north bank of the Humber, near the village of Paull, downstream from Hull in the East Riding of Yorkshire, England.
why_interesting: A fascinating coastal fort overlooking the Humber Estuary.

name: Fort Royal Hill
Wikipedia Extract: Fort Royal Hill is a park in Worcester, England, and the site of the remains of an English Civil War fort.
why_interesting: The hilltop earthworks where Worcester's decisive Civil War battle was fought.

name: Fort Southwick
Wikipedia Extract: Fort Southwick is one of the forts found on Portsdown Hill, which overlooks the naval base of Portsmouth in the county of Hampshire, England.
why_interesting: A major Palmerston fort overlooking Portsmouth Harbour.

name: Henley Fort
Wikipedia Extract: Henley Fort is a Victorian fort near Guildford, Surrey, at the eastern end of the 'Hog's Back' ridge.
why_interesting: A well-preserved Victorian fort hidden in the Surrey Hills.

name: Round Tower (Portsmouth)
Wikipedia Extract: The Round Tower is a fortification at the entrance to Portsmouth Harbour. It is a Grade I listed building.
why_interesting: Portsmouth's iconic medieval defensive tower overlooking the harbour entrance.

name: Square Tower
Wikipedia Extract: The Square Tower is one of the oldest parts of the fortifications of Portsmouth, England. It is a Grade I listed building.
why_interesting: A magnificent medieval artillery tower overlooking Portsmouth Harbour.

name: Bennachie
Wikipedia Extract: Bennachie ( ben-ə-HEE; Scottish Gaelic: Beinn na Cìche) is a range of hills in Aberdeenshire, Scotland.  It has several tops, the highest of which, Oxen Craig, has a height of 528 metres (1,732 ft).
why_interesting: One of Scotland's most famous hillforts, crowning the summit of Bennachie.

name: Caterthun
Wikipedia Extract: Caterthun, or the Caterthuns, is a ridge of hills near the city of Brechin in Angus, Scotland. The Caterthuns are notable for being the site of two Iron Age forts known as the White Caterthun and the Brown Caterthun which are designated as a scheduled monument.
why_interesting: Twin Iron Age hillforts dominating the Angus landscape.

name: Cluny Hill
Wikipedia Extract:
Cluny Hill is a hill on the East side of Forres, Scotland.

At the top of Cluny Hill is Nelson's Tower, built in 1806 to commemorate Admiral Lord Nelson and his victory at Trafalgar.
why_interesting: An Iron Age hillfort overlooking Forres and the Moray coast.

name: Dundarg Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Dundarg Castle is a ruined castle about 2 kilometres (1.2 mi) north-northeast of New Aberdour, Aberdeenshire, Scotland, built within the ramparts of an earlier Iron Age promontory fort. It was described by W. Douglas Simpson as one of the nine castles of the Knuckle, referring to the rocky headland of North-East Aberdeenshire, and by Charles McKean as "Scotland's answer to Tintagel".
why_interesting: The dramatic ruins of a coastal fortress overlooking the North Sea.

name: Dunsinane Hill
Wikipedia Extract: Dunsinane Hill ( dun-SIN-ən) is a hill of the Sidlaws near the village of Collace in Perthshire, Scotland.  It is mentioned in Shakespeare's play Macbeth, in which a vision informs Macbeth that he "shall never vanquished be, until Great Birnam wood to high Dunsinane hill Shall come against him." It is also where the Battle of Dunsinane, a real battle also featured in Macbeth, occurred.
why_interesting: The legendary hill fort associated with Shakespeare's Macbeth.

name: Dùn Galláin
Wikipedia Extract: Dùn Galláin (English: Fort of the Strangers) is a promontory fort located on the Inner Hebridean island of Colonsay, Scotland. The site is located at grid reference NR34869314.
why_interesting: A spectacular Iron Age dun overlooking the Sound of Islay.

name: Eildon Hill
Wikipedia Extract: Eildon Hill lies just south of Melrose, Scotland in the Scottish Borders, overlooking the town. The name is usually pluralised into "the Eildons" or "Eildon Hills", because of its triple peak.
why_interesting: One of Scotland's largest hillforts, with panoramic views over the Borders.

name: Grennan Hill
Wikipedia Extract: Grennan Hill is the site of an Iron Age hill fort outside Penpont in Dumfries and Galloway, Scotland.
why_interesting: A prominent Iron Age hillfort overlooking Galloway.

name: Norman's Law
Wikipedia Extract: Norman's Law is a prominent hill at the far eastern end of the Ochil Fault, Scotland. It sits above the south bank of the River Tay, around four miles north west of Cupar.
why_interesting: A large Iron Age hillfort commanding views across northeast Fife.

name: Castell Dinas
Wikipedia Extract: Castell Dinas is a hillfort and castle in southern Powys, Wales.  At 450 m (1,476 feet) (SO179301) it has the highest castle in England and Wales.
why_interesting: One of Wales' finest Iron Age hillforts, perched high above the Black Mountains.

name: Crug Hywel
Wikipedia Extract: Crug Hywel is an Iron Age Celtic hillfort, with a clearly visible earth and stone ditch and rampart. Crug Hywel is approached by a couple of public footpaths across farmland from Crickhowell and Llanbedr and visited by the Beacons Way.
why_interesting: The impressive Iron Age hillfort towering above Crickhowell.

name: Banwen
Wikipedia Extract: Banwen is a small village in Neath Port Talbot county borough (NPT) in Wales. Banwen is part of the community of Onllwyn along with the village of Onllwyn itself and the adjacent parish of Dyffryn Cellwen.
why_interesting: The earthworks of a Roman fort hidden in the Dulais Valley.

name: Blestium
Wikipedia Extract: Blestium (also Blestio in the Antonine Itinerary (Iter XIII)) was a small fort and iron working centre in the Roman province of Britannia Superior, part of Roman Britain. It has been identified with the site of the later town of Monmouth in south east Wales, located adjoining the confluence of the River Monnow with the River Wye.
why_interesting: The Roman fort that gave rise to the modern town of Monmouth.

name: Burry Holms
Wikipedia Extract: Burry Holms (grid reference SS403926) (Welsh: Ynys Lanwol), a tidal island with the height of (98 feet (30 m)) is at the northern end of Rhossili Bay in the Gower Peninsula, Wales. During spring and summer, Burry Holms is covered by flowers such as thrift and sea campion.
why_interesting: A tidal island hillfort overlooking the spectacular Gower coastline.

name: Canovium
Wikipedia Extract: Canovium was a fort in the Roman province of Britannia. Its site is located at Caerhun in the Conwy valley, in the county borough of Conwy, in North Wales.
why_interesting: The remains of a Roman fort overlooking the River Conwy.

name: Castell Henllys
Wikipedia Extract:
Castell Henllys (Welsh, "castle of the old court") is an archaeological site near Nevern in north Pembrokeshire, Wales.
The Iron Age hillfort has been the subject of an ongoing excavation since the start of the 21st century, accompanied by an exercise in reconstruction archaeology whereby experiments in prehistoric farming have been practised.
why_interesting: A reconstructed Iron Age hillfort bringing Celtic Britain vividly to life.

name: Lavernock Battery
Wikipedia Extract: Lavernock Battery was built at Lavernock Point, Wales on the recommendations of the 1860 Royal Commission during the late 1860s to protect the ports of the Severn Estuary. It was replaced by a new anti-aircraft battery during World War II that was equipped with four heavy anti-aircraft guns.
why_interesting: A Victorian coastal battery overlooking the Bristol Channel.

name: Leucarum
Wikipedia Extract: Leucarum was a coastal auxiliary fort in the Roman province of Britannia. Its remains are located beneath the town of Loughor in the Welsh city of Swansea.
why_interesting: The remains of the Roman fort beneath modern Loughor.

name: Pill Fort
Wikipedia Extract: Pill Fort was a sconce fort located on the northern shore of Milford Haven, Pembrokeshire. It was built by Royalist forces in order to prevent Parliamentarian forces landing at Pembroke Castle, and to protect Royalist forces landing from Ireland.
why_interesting: A compact Victorian fort guarding the Milford Haven Waterway.

name: Popton Fort
Wikipedia Extract:
Popton Fort, a Grade II* Listed Building, is a Palmerston fort completed in 1864 as part of the inner line of defence of Milford Haven together with Fort Hubberstone on the opposite bank.
Work commenced in 1859, only completed in 1864 at a cost of £76,000.
why_interesting: A Victorian artillery fort overlooking Milford Haven.

name: Scoveston Fort
Wikipedia Extract: Scoveston Fort, on the northern shore of Milford Haven, Pembrokeshire, Wales, U.K., is a Grade II listed building which is part of a series of forts built as the inner line of defence of the Haven following the Royal Commission on the Defence of the United Kingdom.
why_interesting: A well-preserved Victorian fort built to defend Milford Haven.

name: South Hook Fort
Wikipedia Extract: South Hook Fort, on the northern shore of Milford Haven, Pembrokeshire, is a Grade II* listed building which belongs to a series of forts built as part of the inner line of defence of the Haven following the Royal Commission on the Defence of the United Kingdom.
why_interesting: A coastal fort overlooking the entrance to Milford Haven.

name: Stack Rock Fort
Wikipedia Extract: Stack Rock Fort is a fort built on a small island in the Milford Haven Waterway, Pembrokeshire, Wales. A 3-gun fort was built between 1850 and 1852, and then upgraded from 1859 to 1871 with a new building that completely encased the original gun tower.
why_interesting: A remarkable sea fort standing on its own rocky island.

name: West Blockhouse Fort
Wikipedia Extract: West Blockhouse Fort is a mid-19th century coastal artillery fort at West Blockhouse Point, a rocky headland near Dale, Pembrokeshire, to the west of Milford Haven in Wales.
why_interesting: The remains of the Roman fort at Brecon.

name: Y Gaer
Wikipedia Extract:
Y Gaer (Latin: Cicucium) is a Roman fort situated near modern-day Brecon in Mid Wales, United Kingdom.
Y Gaer is located at grid reference SO00332966 (Landranger 160).
why_interesting: A spectacular island fort guarding the entrance to Milford Haven.

name: Thorne Island
Wikipedia Extract: Thorne Island is a rocky islet and part of the community of Angle, Pembrokeshire, Wales, with an area of 2 acres (8,100 m2), dominated by a coastal artillery fort built to defend the Milford Haven Waterway in the mid-19th century. It has been the site of a number of shipwrecks, including one in 1894 that was carrying a cargo of Scotch whisky.
why_interesting: The Iron Age hillfort beneath the modern town of Aylesbury.

name: Aylesbury
Wikipedia Extract: Aylesbury ( AYLZ-bər-ee or  ELLZ-bree) is the county town of Buckinghamshire, England. It is located midway between High Wycombe and Milton Keynes.
why_interesting: A well-preserved Iron Age hillfort in the Chiltern Hills.

name: Cholesbury
Wikipedia Extract: Cholesbury (recorded as Chelwardisbyry in the 13th century) is a village in the civil parish of Cholesbury-cum-St. Leonards, in Buckinghamshire, England, on the border with Hertfordshire.
why_interesting: The earthworks of an Iron Age hillfort overlooking Gerrards Cross.

name: Gerrards Cross
Wikipedia Extract: Gerrards Cross is a town and civil parish in Buckinghamshire, England. It is contiguous with Chalfont St Peter, lying immediately south of it.
why_interesting: An Iron Age hillfort overlooking the Vale of Aylesbury.

name: Great and Little Kimble cum Marsh
Wikipedia Extract: Great and Little Kimble cum Marsh is a civil parish in central Buckinghamshire, England. It is located 5 miles (8 km) to the south of Aylesbury.
why_interesting: A dramatic Napoleonic fort overlooking Tor Bay.

name: Berry Head
Wikipedia Extract: Berry Head is a coastal headland that forms the southern boundary of Tor Bay in Devon, England. Lying to the east of the town of Brixham, it is a national nature reserve and a local nature reserve.
why_interesting: The ancient hillfort crowning Cornwall's iconic granite hill.

name: Carn Brea, Redruth
Wikipedia Extract: Carn Brea (Cornish: Karnbre) is a civil parish and hilltop site in Cornwall, England, United Kingdom. The population of Carn Brea including Bosleake and Church Coombe was 8,013 at the 2011 census.
why_interesting: An impressive Iron Age hillfort overlooking the Devon countryside.

name: Cadbury Castle, Devon
Wikipedia Extract: Cadbury Castle is an Iron Age Hillfort close to Bickleigh, Devon, England. It was later encamped by the Parliamentarian forces during the English Civil War under Thomas Fairfax when he laid siege to Bickleigh Castle.
why_interesting: The earthworks of a prehistoric hillfort hidden in Mid Devon.

name: Castle Close
Wikipedia Extract: Castle Close is a circular earthwork located near Stoodleigh in Mid Devon, England at OS grid reference SS937181. It is described on maps as a settlement.
why_interesting: One of Devon's finest surviving Iron Age hillforts.

name: Clovelly Dykes
Wikipedia Extract: Clovelly Dykes is an Iron Age hill fort or earthwork near Clovelly, Devon, England. Situated on the high plateau behind the coast at approx 210 metres above sea level, it is one of the largest and most impressive Early Iron Age hill-forts in Devon.
why_interesting: A well-preserved prehistoric hillfort overlooking the Exe Valley.

name: Cranmore Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Cranmore Castle is an Iron Age earthwork situated on a hillside above the Devon town of Tiverton in south-west England. Its National Grid reference is SS958118.
why_interesting: One of southwest England's most important Iron Age hillforts.

name: Dumpdon Hill
Wikipedia Extract: Dumpdon Hill is an Iron Age Hill Fort near Honiton in Devon. Somewhat overshadowed by its better known neighbour Hembury Fort it is nonetheless as impressive an earthwork.
why_interesting: A spectacular hillfort overlooking the Jurassic Coast.

name: Hembury
Wikipedia Extract: Hembury is a Neolithic causewayed enclosure and Iron Age hillfort near Honiton in Devon. Its history stretches from the late fifth and early fourth millennia BC to the Roman invasion.
why_interesting: The earthworks of an Iron Age hillfort overlooking west Dorset.

name: Abbotsbury Castle
Wikipedia Extract:
Abbotsbury Castle is an Iron Age hillfort in south west Dorset, England, situated on Wears Hill above the village of Abbotsbury, seven miles west of Dorchester and the famous hill fort at Maiden Castle.
It is situated on a high chalk hill overlooking the English Channel, and in its day was the front line of defence from invasion.
why_interesting: A large Iron Age hillfort hidden within Epping Forest.

name: Allington, Dorset
Wikipedia Extract: Allington is a neighbourhood of Bridport in Dorset, England, immediately north-west of Bridport town centre on the west bank of the River Brit. Formerly a separate village and civil parish, Allington and Bridport had grown to be contiguous by the end of the 19th century.
why_interesting: One of Britain's finest Iron Age hillforts, surrounded by ancient beech woodland.

name: Ambresbury Banks
Wikipedia Extract: Ambresbury Banks is the name given to the remains of an Iron Age hill fort in Epping Forest, Essex, England. It lies in 'Long Running & Ambresbury Banks', south of Bell Common and north of Loughton and its neighbouring hillfort Loughton Camp.
why_interesting: The impressive earthworks of Essex's largest Iron Age hillfort.

name: Badbury Rings
Wikipedia Extract: Badbury Rings is an Iron Age hill fort and Scheduled Monument in east Dorset, England. It was in the territory of the Durotriges.
why_interesting: An Iron Age hillfort overlooking Charnwood Forest.

name: Danbury, Essex
Wikipedia Extract: Danbury is a village and civil parish in the Chelmsford district of Essex, England. It is located 33.5 miles (53.9 km) northeast of Charing Cross, London.
why_interesting: A well-preserved Iron Age fort hidden in the Norfolk countryside.

name: Beacon Hill, Leicestershire
Wikipedia Extract: Beacon Hill, near Loughborough, in Leicestershire, England, is a popular country park. It is one of several beacon hills in the United Kingdom.
why_interesting: One of Britain's most spectacular hillforts, commanding panoramic views from the Malvern Hills.

name: Bloodgate Hill Iron Age Fort
Wikipedia Extract: The Bloodgate Hill Iron Age Fort is an Iron Age hill fort in Norfolk, England, situated on a hill above the village of South Creake in the north of the county. The meaning of the name Bloodgate is unknown, but is taken from the road that runs from the fort to the village.
why_interesting: The vast Iron Age hillfort overlooking the Wye Valley.

name: British Camp
Wikipedia Extract: British Camp is an Iron Age hill fort located at the top of Herefordshire Beacon in the Malvern Hills. The hill fort is protected as a Scheduled Ancient Monument and is owned and maintained by Malvern Hills Conservators.
why_interesting: One of Britain's most important Iron Age hillforts, famous for its archaeological discoveries.

name: Credenhill
Wikipedia Extract: Credenhill is a village and civil parish in Herefordshire, England. The population of this civil parish taken at the 2011 Census was 2,271.
why_interesting: The island refuge where Alfred the Great regrouped against the Vikings.

name: Danebury
Wikipedia Extract: Danebury is an Iron Age hillfort in Hampshire, England, about 19 kilometres (12 mi) north-west of Winchester (grid reference SU323376). The site, covering 5 hectares (12 acres), was excavated by Barry Cunliffe in the 1970s.
why_interesting: The prominent Iron Age hillfort overlooking Shrewsbury.

name: Athelney
Wikipedia Extract: Athelney is a village located between the villages of Burrowbridge and East Lyng in Somerset, England. The name is believed to be derived from the Old English æþeling meaning "prince" + -ey meaning "isle".
why_interesting: One of Britain's largest hillforts, with panoramic views across Northamptonshire.

name: Bayston Hill
Wikipedia Extract: Bayston Hill is a village and civil parish in Shropshire, England. It is 3 miles (5 km) south of the county town Shrewsbury and located on the main A49 road, the Shrewsbury to Hereford road.
why_interesting: A dramatic coastal headland crowned by Iron Age earthworks and Victorian fortifications.

name: Borough Hill
Wikipedia Extract: Borough Hill is a hill to the east of the town of Daventry in the English county of Northamptonshire. It is over 200 metres (660 ft) above sea level and dominates the surrounding area.
why_interesting: The highest hill in Shropshire, crowned by prehistoric earthworks.

name: Brean Down
Wikipedia Extract:
Brean Down is a promontory off the coast of Somerset, England, standing 318 feet (97 m) high and extending 1+1⁄2 miles (2.5 kilometres) into the Bristol Channel at the eastern end of Bridgwater Bay between Weston-super-Mare and Burnham-on-Sea.
Made of Carboniferous Limestone, it is a continuation of the Mendip Hills.
why_interesting: An impressive Iron Age hillfort overlooking the Somerset Levels.

name: Brown Clee Hill
Wikipedia Extract: Brown Clee Hill is the highest hill in the rural English county of Shropshire, at 540 metres (1,770 ft)  above sea level. It is one of the Clee Hills, and is in the Shropshire Hills Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty.
why_interesting: An Iron Age promontory fort overlooking the Bristol Channel.

name: Compton Dundon
Wikipedia Extract: Compton Dundon is a village and civil parish in Somerset, England, lying beside King's Sedgemoor and the Polden Hills, 5 miles (8 km) south of Glastonbury and 4 miles (6 km) north of Somerton. The village has a population of 705.
why_interesting: A beautifully preserved Iron Age hillfort hidden in the Mendip Hills.

name: Daw's Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Daw's Castle (or Dart's Castle or Dane's Castle) is a sea cliff hillfort just west of Watchet, a harbour town in Somerset, England. It is a Scheduled Monument.
why_interesting: An Iron Age hillfort dramatically overlooking the Bristol Channel.

name: Dolebury Warren
Wikipedia Extract: Dolebury Warren (also known as Dolebury Camp) is a 90.6-hectare (224-acre) biological Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI) and ancient monument near the villages of Churchill and Rowberrow in North Somerset, part of South West England. It is owned by the National Trust, who acquired the freehold in 1983, and managed by the Avon Wildlife Trust.
why_interesting: One of the Mendip Hills' finest Iron Age hillforts with panoramic views.

name: Barbury Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Barbury Castle is a scheduled hillfort in Wiltshire, England, about 5.5 miles (9 km) south of Swindon.
why_interesting: A beautifully preserved Iron Age hillfort on the Marlborough Downs.

name: Castle Ring
Wikipedia Extract:
Castle Ring is an Iron Age hill fort, situated high up on the southern edge of Cannock Chase (The Chase), Staffordshire, England.
It is the highest point on The Chase with an elevation of 242 metres (794 ft).
why_interesting: A prominent Iron Age hillfort crowning Cannock Chase.

name: Chanctonbury Ring
Wikipedia Extract: Chanctonbury Ring is a prehistoric hill fort atop Chanctonbury Hill on the South Downs, on the border of the civil parishes of Washington and Wiston in the English county of West Sussex. A ridgeway, now part of the South Downs Way, runs along the hill.
why_interesting: A legendary Iron Age hillfort surrounded by ancient beech woodland and local folklore.

name: Cissbury Ring
Wikipedia Extract: Cissbury Ring is an 84.2-hectare (208-acre) biological Site of Special Scientific Interest north of Worthing in West Sussex. It is owned by the National Trust  and is designated a Scheduled monument for its Neolithic flint mine and Iron Age hillfort.
why_interesting: One of Britain's largest Iron Age hillforts, offering spectacular views across Sussex.

name: Berry Mound
Wikipedia Extract:
Berry Mound is an Iron Age hill fort in the Bromsgrove district of Worcestershire, near Shirley, West Midlands, on the outskirts of Birmingham. It has been dated to the 1st or 2nd century BC.
The fort covers 11 acres (4.5 ha), measuring 450 ft (140 m) from north to south and 200 ft (61 m) from east to west.
why_interesting: The impressive earthworks of an Iron Age hillfort overlooking Birmingham.

name: Bredon Hill
Wikipedia Extract: Bredon Hill is a hill located in Worcestershire, England, south-west of Evesham in the Vale of Evesham. The summit of the hill is in the parish of Kemerton, and it extends over parts of eight other parishes (listed below).
why_interesting: A vast Iron Age hillfort commanding views across the Vale of Evesham.

name: Carl Wark
Wikipedia Extract: Carl Wark (sometimes Carl's Wark) is a rocky promontory on Hathersage Moor in the Peak District National Park, just inside the boundary of Sheffield, England. The promontory is faced by vertical cliffs on all but one side, which is protected by a prehistoric embankment.
why_interesting: A remarkable gritstone hillfort in the heart of the Peak District.

name: Castle Hill, Huddersfield
Wikipedia Extract: Castle Hill is a scheduled ancient monument in Almondbury overlooking Huddersfield in the Metropolitan Borough of Kirklees, West Yorkshire, England. The hilltop has been settled for at least 4,000 years.
why_interesting: The iconic hilltop monument and Iron Age hillfort overlooking Huddersfield.

name: Drakelow Hillfort
Wikipedia Extract: Drakelow Hillfort is a small multivallate Iron Age hillfort, located on a promontory (known as Drakelow Hill) at Drakelow at the southern end of Kinver Edge, in the civil parish of Wolverley and Cookley, Worcestershire.  The hillfort is a scheduled monument.
why_interesting: The earthworks of an Iron Age hillfort overlooking the Severn Valley.

name: Maiden Castle, North Yorkshire
Wikipedia Extract: Maiden Castle is a settlement in Grinton, North Yorkshire (grid reference SE02189808) which probably dates from the Iron Age. It is listed as a scheduled monument.
why_interesting: The impressive earthworks of an Iron Age hillfort overlooking Wensleydale.

name: Stanwick Iron Age Fortifications
Wikipedia Extract: The Stanwick Iron Age Fortifications (also known as 'Stanwick Camp'), a huge Iron Age hill fort, sometimes but not always considered an oppidum, comprising over 9 kilometres (5.6 mi) of ditches and ramparts enclosing approximately 300 hectares (740 acres) of land, are situated in Richmondshire, North Yorkshire, England. Whether Stanwick was the stronghold of Venutius or Cartimandua, or perhaps of them both for a brief time before their acrimonious split some time after 51 AD, it is certain that this settlement was one of the most important in Brigantia, the Brigantes kingdom during the early stages of the Roman occupation of Britain.
why_interesting: One of Britain's largest Iron Age enclosed settlements.

name: White Sheet Hill
Wikipedia Extract: White Sheet Hill, also known as Whitesheet Hill, is a hill in the English county of Wiltshire. As one of the most westerly areas of downland in Britain the area is noted for its chalky farmland which contains a rich variety of rare and protected fauna and flora.
why_interesting: A prominent Iron Age hillfort with sweeping views across Wiltshire.

name: Wincobank (hill fort)
Wikipedia Extract: Wincobank  (grid reference SK377910) is an Iron Age hill fort near Wincobank in Sheffield, England.
why_interesting: A substantial Iron Age hillfort overlooking Sheffield.

name: Yarnbury Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Yarnbury Castle is the site of a multiphase, multivallate Iron Age hillfort near the village of Steeple Langford, Wiltshire, England. The site covers an area of 28.5 acres (11.5 ha), and was extensively surveyed and investigated by the Royal Commission on the Historical Monuments of England in 1991, with finds of Iron Age and Romano-British pottery, Iron Age and Roman coins, and burials of human remains.
why_interesting: One of Wiltshire's finest surviving Iron Age hillforts.

name: Chesters Hill Fort
Wikipedia Extract: Chesters Hill Fort is an Iron Age hill fort in East Lothian, Scotland. It lies on the north facing slope of the Drem hills, 1 mile (2 kilometres) south of the small village of Drem, 1+1⁄2 mi (2.5 km) east of Ballencrieff Castle, 2+1⁄2 mi (4 km) north of Haddington, and 2 mi (3 km) west of Athelstaneford.
why_interesting: A well-preserved Iron Age hillfort overlooking East Lothian.

name: Rubers Law
Wikipedia Extract: Rubers Law (or locally probably more often Ruberslaw) is a prominent, conical hill in the Scottish Borders area of south-east Scotland. It stands on the south bank of the River Teviot, between the towns of Hawick and Jedburgh, and south of the village of Denholm.
why_interesting: A prominent Borders hillfort with panoramic views across Teviotdale.

name: Torr a'Chaisteal
Wikipedia Extract: Torr a'Chaisteal (or Torr a'Chaisteil) is an Iron Age fort (dun), located about 1 mile (2 kilometres) northeast of the village of Sliddery, on the Isle of Arran in Scotland (grid reference NR92172326).
why_interesting: An Iron Age hillfort overlooking the Kintyre peninsula.

name: Trusty's Hill
Wikipedia Extract:
Trusty's Hill is a small vitrified hillfort about a mile to the west of the present-day town of Gatehouse of Fleet, in the parish of Anwoth in the Stewartry district of Dumfries and Galloway.
The site is notable for a carved Pictish stone located near the entrance to the fort, one of only a handful of such stones found outside the core Pictish heartland of North-East Scotland.
why_interesting: A remarkable Pictish hillfort famed for its carved rock art.

name: Wallace's House
Wikipedia Extract:
Wallace's House is an earthen rampart, located near Lochmaben, Scotland, that is associated with William Wallace.
The promontory fort is a scheduled item.
why_interesting: A prehistoric defended settlement overlooking Annandale.

name: White Meldon
Wikipedia Extract: White Meldon is a prehistoric site, a hillfort near the village of Lyne and about 4 miles (6 km) west of Peebles, in the Scottish Borders, Scotland. It is a Scheduled Monument.
why_interesting: A striking Iron Age hillfort overlooking the Tweed Valley.

name: Breidden Hill
Wikipedia Extract: Breidden Hill is a steep-sided hill in Powys, Wales, near the town of Welshpool.  It is immediately surrounded by the villages of Trewern, Middletown, Criggion, Crew Green and Llandrinio.
why_interesting: One of the finest hillforts on the Welsh border, with far-reaching views.

name: Burfa Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Burfa Castle (also known as Burfa Hillfort, Burfa Bank Hillfort, or Burfa Camp) is an Iron Age hillfort near the village of Old Radnor, Radnorshire in Powys, Wales. The site is a scheduled monument described as a prehistoric defensive hillfort, and was included in an inventory of monuments by 1913.
why_interesting: The earthwork remains of a Norman motte overlooking the Wye Valley.

name: Dinas Powys hillfort
Wikipedia Extract: The Dinas Powys hillfort is an Iron Age hillfort near Dinas Powys, Glamorgan, Wales. It is just one of several thousand hillforts to have been constructed around Great Britain during the British Iron Age, for reasons that are still debatable.
why_interesting: One of Wales' largest and most important Iron Age hillforts.

name: Ffridd Faldwyn, Montgomery
Wikipedia Extract: Ffridd Faldwyn is an Iron Age hillfort in northern Powys, in the former county of Montgomeryshire, It is sited on a prominent hill west of Montgomery, close to but higher than Montgomery Castle, overlooking the River Severn. It is one of the largest hill-forts in Wales.
why_interesting: A substantial Iron Age hillfort overlooking Montgomery.

name: Banna (Birdoswald)
Wikipedia Extract: Birdoswald Roman Fort, known to the Romans as Banna, was one of the 16 forts on Hadrian's Wall. Built in the 2nd century AD, Banna, as a site, continued to be used well beyond Roman occupation.
why_interesting: One of Hadrian's Wall's best-preserved Roman forts with an outstanding visitor centre.

name: Hardknott Roman Fort
Wikipedia Extract: Hardknott Roman Fort is an archeological site, the remains of the Roman fort Mediobogdum, located on the western side of the challenging Hardknott Pass in the English Lake District. The fort was built between 120 and 138 on a rocky spur, and was initially garrisoned by a detachment of the Cohors IV Delmatarum from the Dalmatian coast (in modern Croatia).
why_interesting: England's highest Roman fort, reached via one of Britain's steepest mountain roads.

name: High Street (Lake District)
Wikipedia Extract: High Street is a fell in the English Lake District. At 828 metres (2,717 ft), its summit is the highest point in the far eastern part of the national park.
why_interesting: A spectacular Roman road crossing the highest fells in the Lake District.

name: Milecastle 48
Wikipedia Extract: Milecastle 48 (Poltross Burn) is a milecastle on Hadrian's Wall (grid reference NY6340666195).  Its remains lie near the village of Gilsland in Cumbria where it was historically known as "The King's Stables", owing to the well-preserved interior walls.
why_interesting: A remarkably well-preserved milecastle on Hadrian's Wall.

name: Ardotalia
Wikipedia Extract:
Ardotalia (from British Celtic for "high dark hill"), also known as Melandra or Melandra Castle, is a Roman fort in Gamesley, near Glossop in Derbyshire, England.

Ardotalia was constructed by Cohors Primae Frisiavonum—The First Cohort of Frisiavones.
why_interesting: The impressive remains of the Roman fort guarding the Woodhead Pass.

name: Corbridge Lion
Wikipedia Extract: The Corbridge Lion, Northumberland, England, is an ancient Roman free-standing sandstone sculpture of a male lion standing on a prone animal (possibly a deer) on a semi-cylindrical coping stone base. Measuring 0.95m in length by 0.36m in width and 0.87m high, it was originally a piece of decorative funerary ornamentation from a tomb.
why_interesting: The famous Roman lion sculpture discovered at Corbridge Roman Town.

name: Durnovaria
Wikipedia Extract: Durnovaria is a suggested spelling for the Latin form of the name of the Roman town of Dorchester in the modern English county of Dorset, amended from the actually observed Durnonovaria. Upon the assumption that the name was originally Brythonic, it is suggested that the first element in the name, *durno- may mean "fist" like (Welsh dwrn ‘fist, knob’) and the second may be related to Old Irish fáir ~ fóir denoting a confined area or den.
why_interesting: The Roman town beneath modern Dorchester, once the tribal capital of the Durotriges.

name: Glevum
Wikipedia Extract: Glevum (or, more formally, Colonia Nervia Glevensium, or occasionally Glouvia) was originally a Roman fort in Roman Britain that became a "colonia" of retired legionaries in AD 97. Today, it is known as Gloucester, in the English county of Gloucestershire.
why_interesting: The Roman city beneath modern Gloucester, founded as a legionary fortress.

name: Calcaria
Wikipedia Extract: Calcaria was a town in the Roman province of Britannia. Today, it is known as Tadcaster, located in the English county of North Yorkshire.
why_interesting: The Roman town beneath modern Tadcaster, once an important military settlement.

name: Coria (Corbridge)
Wikipedia Extract: Coria was a fort and town 2.5 miles (4.0 km) south of Hadrian's Wall, in the Roman province of Britannia. It was strategically located on the junction of a major Roman north–south road (Dere Street) with the River Tyne and the Roman Stanegate road, which was also the first frontier line which ran east–west between Coria and Luguvalium (the modern Carlisle).
why_interesting: One of Britain's best-preserved Roman towns, with impressive standing remains.

name: Costa Beck
Wikipedia Extract: Costa Beck is a small river in North Yorkshire, England. It also lends its name to an archaeological site.
why_interesting: The Roman road and bridge crossing the North York Moors.

name: Isurium Brigantum
Wikipedia Extract: Isurium or Isurium of the Brigantes (Latin: Isurium Brigantum) was a Roman fort and town in the province of Britannia at the site of present-day Aldborough in North Yorkshire, England, in the United Kingdom. Its remains—the Aldborough Roman Site—are in the care of English Heritage.

name: Magnis (Carvoran)
Wikipedia Extract: Magnis or Magna was a Roman fort near Hadrian's Wall in northern Britain. Its ruins are now known as Carvoran Roman Fort and are located near Carvoran, Northumberland, in northern England.
why_interesting: One of Britain's best-preserved Roman forts along Hadrian's Wall.

name: Alfred's Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Alfred's Castle is a small Iron Age hill fort, situated at grid reference SU277822, behind Ashdown Park in the civil parish of Ashbury in Oxfordshire (formerly Berkshire). It lies 2–3 km south of the Ridgeway and is protected as a Scheduled Ancient Monument.
why_interesting: An Iron Age hillfort later reused during the Roman period.

name: Faversham Stone Chapel
