Wikipedia Extract:
Kingston Lacy is a country house and estate near Wimborne Minster, Dorset, England. It was for many years the family seat of the Bankes family who lived nearby at Corfe Castle until its destruction in the English Civil War after its incumbent owners, Sir John Bankes and Dame Mary, had remained loyal to Charles I.
The house was built between 1663 and 1665 by Ralph Bankes, son of Sir John Bankes, to a design by the architect Sir Roger Pratt.
why_interesting: Grand Bankes family mansion with an exceptional Egyptian collection and the Philae Obelisk.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Kingston Maurward House
Wikipedia Extract: Kingston Maurward House is a large Grade I listed Georgian English country house set in a 750-acre (3 square km) estate in Dorset situated in the Frome valley two miles east of Dorchester.
why_interesting: Early Georgian mansion later faced in Portland stone, reportedly following advice from George III.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Kingston Russell House
Wikipedia Extract: Kingston Russell House is a large mansion house and manor near Long Bredy in Dorset, England, west of Dorchester.  The present house dates from the late 17th century but in 1730 was clad in a white Georgian stone facade.
why_interesting: Grade I-listed country house and birthplace of Trafalgar captain Sir Thomas Masterman Hardy.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Max Gate
Wikipedia Extract: Max Gate is the former home of Thomas Hardy and is located on the outskirts of Dorchester, Dorset, England. It was designed and built by Thomas Hardy for his own use in 1885 and he lived there until his death in 1928.
why_interesting: Thomas Hardy designed this red-brick home and wrote several of his greatest novels there.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Bateman's
Wikipedia Extract: Bateman's is a 17th-century house located in Burwash, East Sussex, England. It was the home of Rudyard Kipling from 1902 until his death in 1936.
why_interesting: Rudyard Kipling's Jacobean home for over 30 years, preserved with his books and personal belongings.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Burton Agnes Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Burton Agnes Hall is an Elizabethan manor house in the village of Burton Agnes, near Driffield in the East Riding of Yorkshire, England. It was built by Sir Henry Griffith in 1601–10 to designs attributed to Robert Smythson.
why_interesting: Elizabethan family home renowned for carved interiors and ownership by the same family for centuries.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Burton Agnes Manor House
Wikipedia Extract:
Burton Agnes Manor House is an English Heritage property, located in the village of Burton Agnes, East Riding of Yorkshire, England only a few yards away from the newer Burton Agnes Hall. 
It is a surviving example of a Norman manor house with a well-preserved Norman undercroft; a hall house that was later encased in 18th-century brickwork.
why_interesting: Norman manor house built around 1173, among England's oldest surviving domestic buildings.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Burton Constable Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Burton Constable Hall is a large Elizabethan country house in England, with 18th- and 19th-century interiors and a fine 18th-century cabinet of curiosities. The hall, a Grade I listed building, is set in a park designed by Capability Brown with an area of 300 acres (1.2 km2).
why_interesting: Elizabethan hall displaying a 60-foot sperm-whale skeleton connected with Herman Melville's Moby-Dick.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Abbotswick
Wikipedia Extract: Abbotswick, also known as Abbotswick Hall, is a small English country house at Navestock Side in the English county of Essex. The house, which has a well-timbered garden with a small lake, dates from about 1800 but was rebuilt early in the 20th century.
why_interesting: Former Essex country house now serving as a peaceful Catholic retreat centre.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Audley End House
Wikipedia Extract: Audley End House is an early 17th-century English country house near to Saffron Walden in north-west Essex. The Jacobean house was built by the first Earl of Suffolk on the site of a Benedictine monastery that had been awarded to his grandfather, chancellor Thomas Audley, during the dissolution of the monasteries.
why_interesting: Once a Jacobean palace “in all but name”, later used to train wartime Polish special agents.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Creeksea Place
Wikipedia Extract: Creeksea Place is located near to the town of Burnham-on-Crouch in the Essex countryside of eastern England. Originally built in 1569, the estate retains many original internal and external features, with an original walled-garden and untouched orchard, where the BBC’s adaptation of Great Expectations was filmed.
why_interesting: Red-brick Elizabethan house completed in 1569, set among woodland and ornamental lakes.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Acton Court
Wikipedia Extract: Acton Court is the historic manor house of the manor of Iron Acton in Gloucestershire, England. It is a grade I listed building of Tudor architecture and was recently restored.
why_interesting: Rare Tudor state apartments built in just nine months for Henry VIII and Anne Boleyn's 1535 visit.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Calcot Manor
Wikipedia Extract: Calcot Manor is a historic building in Calcot, three and a half miles west of Tetbury on A 4135 in Gloucestershire, England, near the junction of roads A46 and A4135 (National Grid Reference ST 841180 94891). The original building was established in approximately 1300 AD by Henry of Kingswood as a tithe barn annex of Kingswood Abbey.
why_interesting: Historic Cotswold manor with medieval monastic barns, now a renowned country-house hotel and spa.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Chavenage House
Wikipedia Extract: Chavenage House, Tetbury, Gloucestershire is an English country house. A Grade I listed building, it is described in the Gloucestershire: Cotswolds volume of the Pevsner Buildings of England series as "the ideal sixteenth-century Cotswold stone manor house".
why_interesting: Elizabethan manor seen in Poldark and Rivals, with Civil War relics and celebrated ghost stories.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Dyrham Park
Wikipedia Extract: Dyrham Park () is a baroque English country house in an ancient deer park near the village of Dyrham in South Gloucestershire, England. The house, with the attached orangery and stable block, is a Grade I listed building, while the park is Grade II* listed on the National Register of Historic Parks and Gardens.
why_interesting: Baroque mansion created for William Blathwayt, filled with Dutch art and surrounded by historic parkland.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Bramall Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Bramall Hall is a manor house in Bramhall, Stockport, Greater Manchester, England. Largely Tudor in design, its oldest parts date from the 14th century, with additions from the 16th and 19th centuries.
why_interesting: One of Cheshire's grandest black-and-white timber-framed halls, with history stretching back before 1066.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Flixton House
Wikipedia Extract: Flixton House was built in 1806 by the Wright family, who had become wealthy land owners in Flixton. It is a Queen Anne revival style country house, in Flemish bond brick, with neo-classical portico and fanlight.
why_interesting: Georgian manor linked to the 1826 Flixton Footpath Battle over blocked public rights of way.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Amport House
Wikipedia Extract: Amport House is a country house near the village of Amport, Andover, Hampshire, England. It is a Grade II listed building.
why_interesting: 1857 mansion by William Burn, complemented by formal gardens designed by Lutyens and Gertrude Jekyll.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Bramshill House
Wikipedia Extract: Bramshill House, in Bramshill, northeast Hampshire, England, is one of the largest and most important Jacobean prodigy house mansions in England. It was built in the early 17th century by the 11th Baron Zouche of Harringworth but was partly destroyed by fire a few years later.
why_interesting: One of England's largest Jacobean houses, built from 1605 with rare surviving early water gardens.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Broadlands
Wikipedia Extract: Broadlands is a country house located in the civil parish of Romsey Extra, near the town of Romsey in the Test Valley district of Hampshire, England. Its formal gardens and historic landscape are Grade II* listed on the Register of Historic Parks and Gardens.
why_interesting: Palladian riverside mansion associated with Lord Mountbatten and used by several royal couples for honeymoons.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Exbury Gardens
Wikipedia Extract: Exbury Gardens is a 200-acre (81 ha) informal woodland garden in Hampshire, England, with large collections of rhododendrons, azaleas and camellias, and is often considered the finest garden of its type in the United Kingdom. Exbury holds the national collection of Nyssa (Tupelo) and Oxydendrum under the National Plant Collection scheme run by the Plant Heritage charity.
why_interesting: Rothschild woodland gardens famed for rhododendrons, azaleas and a narrow-gauge steam railway.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Berrington Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Berrington Hall is a country house located about 3 miles (5 km) north of Leominster, Herefordshire, England. During the 20th century it was the seat of the Cawley family.
why_interesting: Neoclassical mansion overlooking Capability Brown's final completed landscape.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Hursley House
Wikipedia Extract: Hursley House is an 18th-century Queen Anne style mansion in Hursley, near Winchester in the English county of Hampshire. The building is Grade II* listed.
why_interesting: Historic country house now home to IBM's major UK research and development laboratories.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: King's House, Winchester
Wikipedia Extract: The King's House in Winchester was a late 17th-century planned royal palace in the English county of Hampshire. Winchester had been the capital of Wessex and England in Anglo-Saxon times, but became a backwater after the Norman Conquest of England.
why_interesting: Site of Charles II's unfinished royal palace, designed by Christopher Wren and later absorbed into military barracks.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Ashridge
Wikipedia Extract: Ashridge is a country estate and stately home in Hertfordshire, England. It is situated in the Chiltern Hills, an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, about 2 miles (3.2 km) north of Berkhamsted and 23 miles (37 km) north west of London.
why_interesting: Grand Gothic Revival mansion built on a former monastery site and now used as a business school.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Bayfordbury
Wikipedia Extract: Bayfordbury, Hertfordshire, is a large Grade II* listed country house with surrounding parkland, and the location of a University of Hertfordshire campus, housing its biology/geography field station and observatory.
why_interesting: Georgian country estate now housing the University of Hertfordshire's observatory and atmospheric research facilities.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Bhaktivedanta Manor
Wikipedia Extract: Bhaktivedanta Manor is a Gaudiya Vaishnava Hindu temple set in the Hertfordshire countryside of England, in the village of Letchmore Heath near Watford. The Manor is owned and run by the International Society for Krishna Consciousness (ISKCON), better known as the Hare Krishna movement.
why_interesting: George Harrison donated this Tudor-style manor to the Hare Krishna movement in 1973.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Brocket Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Brocket Hall is a neo-classical country house set in a large park at the western side of the urban area of Welwyn Garden City in Hertfordshire, England. The estate includes two golf courses and seven smaller listed buildings, apart from the main house.
why_interesting: Georgian mansion associated with prime ministers Lord Melbourne and Lord Palmerston.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Buntingford Manor House
Wikipedia Extract: Buntingford Manor House is an 18th-century building in the town of Buntingford, in Hertfordshire, England. It is a Grade II listed building.
why_interesting: Historic manor house reflecting Buntingford's long development as a Hertfordshire market town.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Cassiobury House
Wikipedia Extract: Cassiobury House was a country house in Cassiobury Park, Watford, England. It was the ancestral seat of the Earls of Essex.
why_interesting: Former seat of the Earls of Essex, demolished in 1927, with its parkland surviving at Watford.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Hatfield House
Wikipedia Extract:
Hatfield House is a Grade I listed country house set in a large park, the Great Park, on the eastern side of Hatfield, Hertfordshire, England.
The present Jacobean house, a leading example of the prodigy house, was built in 1611 by Robert Cecil, 1st Earl of Salisbury and Chief Minister to James I. It is a prime example of Jacobean architecture.
why_interesting: Jacobean prodigy house built in 1611 beside the childhood home of Elizabeth I.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Knebworth House
Wikipedia Extract: Knebworth House is an English country house in the parish of Knebworth in Hertfordshire, England. It is a Grade II* listed building.
why_interesting: Gothic mansion famed for the Lytton family and decades of major outdoor rock concerts.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Moor Park (house)
Wikipedia Extract: Moor Park is a Neo-Palladian mansion set within several hundred acres of parkland to the south-east of Rickmansworth in Hertfordshire, England. It is called Moor Park Mansion because it is in the old park of the Manor of the More, a 16th-century palace.
why_interesting: Palladian mansion with lavish painted interiors, now serving as a prestigious golf clubhouse.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Chartwell
Wikipedia Extract: Chartwell is a country house near Westerham, Kent, in South East England. For over forty years, it was the home of Sir Winston Churchill.
why_interesting: Winston Churchill's beloved family home, preserved with his painting studio, gardens and personal belongings.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Chevening
Wikipedia Extract: Chevening House () is a large country house in the parish of Chevening in Kent, England. Built between 1617 and 1630 to a design reputedly by Inigo Jones and greatly extended after 1717, it is a Grade I listed building.
why_interesting: Seventeenth-century estate serving as an official country residence for the Foreign Secretary and senior ministers.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Cobham Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Cobham Hall is an English country house in the county of Kent, England. The grade I listed building is one of the largest and most important houses in Kent, re-built as an Elizabethan prodigy house by William Brooke, 10th Baron Cobham (1527–1597).
why_interesting: Elizabethan and Jacobean mansion set within parkland landscaped by Capability Brown.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Cobham Hall School
Wikipedia Extract: Cobham Hall School is a private co-educational day and boarding school in the English parish of Cobham, Kent, for girls and boys aged 11-19. It is a Round Square school and a member of the Girls' Schools Association.
why_interesting: Independent school occupying Cobham Hall's historic mansion and Capability Brown parkland.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Astley Hall, Chorley
Wikipedia Extract: Astley Hall is a country house in Chorley, Lancashire, England. The building is now owned by the town and is known as Astley Hall Museum and Art Gallery.
why_interesting: Jacobean mansion known for richly decorated interiors and its connections with the English Civil War.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Capernwray Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Capernwray Hall is a former country house situated 3 miles (4.8 km) east-northeast of Carnforth, Lancashire, England, and is currently used as a Christian Bible school and holiday centre. The house is recorded in the National Heritage List for England as a designated Grade II* listed building.
why_interesting: Victorian mansion that has housed an international Christian Bible school since 1947.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Ightham Mote
Wikipedia Extract: Ightham Mote (), at Ightham, is a medieval moated manor house in Kent, England. The architectural writer John Newman describes it as "the most complete small medieval manor house in the county".
why_interesting: One of England's best-preserved medieval moated manor houses, with architecture spanning several centuries.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Beaumanor Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Beaumanor Hall is a stately home with a park in the small village of Woodhouse on the edge of the Charnwood Forest, near the town of Loughborough in Leicestershire, England. The present hall was built in 1842–1848 by architect William Railton for the Herrick family, with previous halls dating back to the 14th century.
why_interesting: Country estate used as a secret wartime signals-intelligence station intercepting enemy communications.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Chingle Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Chingle Hall is a grade II listed manor house in the township of Whittingham near Preston, England.
why_interesting: Thirteenth-century moated manor often described as one of England's most haunted houses.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Gawthorpe Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Gawthorpe Hall is an Elizabethan country house on the banks of the River Calder, in Ightenhill, a civil parish in the Borough of Burnley, Lancashire, England. Its estate extends into Padiham, with the Stockbridge Drive entrance situated there.
why_interesting: Elizabethan house containing an important textile collection and strong connections with the Brontë family.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Hoghton Tower
Wikipedia Extract: Hoghton Tower is a fortified manor house two-thirds of a mile (1 km) east of the village of Hoghton, Lancashire, England, and stands on a hilltop site on the highest point in the area. It takes its name from the de Hoghton family, its historical owners since at least the 12th century.
why_interesting: Fortified hilltop manor visited by James I and his court in 1617.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Ayscoughfee Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Ayscoughfee Hall   is a grade I listed building and modest associated parkland in central Spalding, Lincolnshire, England, and is a landmark on the fen tour.
why_interesting: Late-medieval merchant's house now serving as a museum beside formal gardens and a war memorial.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Belton House
Wikipedia Extract: Belton House is a Grade I listed country house in the parish of Belton near Grantham in Lincolnshire, England, built between 1685 and 1687 by Sir John Brownlow, 3rd Baronet. It is surrounded by formal gardens and a series of avenues leading to follies within a larger wooded park.
why_interesting: Classic Restoration country house used as Rosings Park in the 1995 BBC Pride and Prejudice.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Bosworth Hall, Market Bosworth
Wikipedia Extract: Bosworth Hall is a historic country house and Grade II* listed building in the rural town of Market Bosworth in Leicestershire, England, now known as the Bosworth Hall Hotel. It was the country seat of the Dixie family (baronets of Bosworth) for nearly three hundred years.
why_interesting: Seventeenth-century country house associated for generations with the Dixie family, now operating as a hotel.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Branston Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Branston Hall is a country house in the village of Branston, Lincolnshire, England. The hall, a Grade II listed building, is set in 88 acres (3.56 square kilometres) of wooded parkland and lakes.
why_interesting: Victorian country house in landscaped grounds, later adapted for institutional and hospitality use.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Brooksby Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Brooksby Hall is a late–16th-century manor house on 3.2 square kilometres (800 acres) of land between Leicester and Melton Mowbray. Situated 13 kilometres (8.1 mi) northeast of Leicester, the hall and the neighbouring church of St Michael and All Angels are the last remnants of the medieval village of Brooksby, which was founded during the period of the Danelaw in the 9th century AD. In the 15th and 16th centuries Brooksby was depopulated by enclosures carried out by the estate's owners, which turned its cultivated land into sheep pastures in order to profit from a boom in wool.
why_interesting: Birthplace of George Villiers, the influential favourite of James I and first Duke of Buckingham.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Doddington Hall, Lincolnshire
Wikipedia Extract: Doddington Hall is, from the outside, an Elizabethan prodigy house or mansion complete with walled courtyards and a gabled gatehouse. Inside it was largely updated in the 1760s.
why_interesting: Robert Smythson-designed Elizabethan hall completed in 1600 and still occupied by the same family.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Addington Palace
Wikipedia Extract: Addington Palace is an 18th-century mansion in Addington located within the London Borough of Croydon. It was built close to the site of an earlier manor house belonging to the Leigh family.
why_interesting: Former country residence of the Archbishops of Canterbury during the 19th century.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Fulham Palace
Wikipedia Extract: Fulham Palace is a museum and former bishop's palace. It lies on the north bank of the River Thames in Fulham, London, previously in the former English county of Middlesex.
why_interesting: Home of the Bishops of London for over 1,300 years, with gardens beside the Thames.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Ham House
Wikipedia Extract: Ham House is a 17th-century house set in formal gardens on the bank of the River Thames in Ham, south of Richmond in the London Borough of Richmond upon Thames. The original house was completed in 1610 by Thomas Vavasour, an Elizabethan courtier and Knight Marshal to James I. It was then leased, and later bought, by William Murray, a close friend and supporter of Charles I. The English Civil War saw the house and much of the estate sequestrated, but Murray's wife Catherine regained them on payment of a fine.
why_interesting: Exceptionally complete 17th-century house preserving lavish interiors created by the Duke and Duchess of Lauderdale.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Hampton Court Palace
Wikipedia Extract:
Hampton Court Palace is a Grade I listed royal palace in the London Borough of Richmond upon Thames, 12 miles (19 kilometres) southwest and upstream of central London on the River Thames.
The building of the palace began in 1514 for Cardinal Thomas Wolsey, Archbishop of York and the chief minister of Henry VIII. In 1529, as Wolsey fell from favour, the cardinal gave the palace to the king to try to save his own life, which he knew was now in grave danger due to Henry VIII's deepening frustration and anger.
why_interesting: Henry VIII's great Tudor palace, famous for royal apartments, vast kitchens and its historic maze.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Kensington Palace
Wikipedia Extract: Kensington Palace is a royal residence situated within Kensington Gardens in the Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea in London, England. It has served as a residence for the British royal family since the 17th century and is currently the official London residence of several royals, including the Prince and Princess of Wales, the Duke and Duchess of Gloucester, the Duke of Kent, Prince and Princess Michael of Kent, and Princess Eugenie alongside her husband, Jack Brooksbank.
why_interesting: Royal palace where Queen Victoria was born, with apartments exploring generations of royal residents.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Kew Palace
Wikipedia Extract: Kew Palace is a British royal palace within the grounds of Kew Gardens on the banks of the River Thames. Originally a large complex, few elements of it survive.
why_interesting: Britain's smallest royal palace, closely associated with George III and Queen Charlotte.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Allerton Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Allerton Hall is a Grade II* listed former country house in Clarke's Gardens, Allerton, Merseyside, England. It was built in about 1736 for the Hardman family.
why_interesting: Eighteenth-century mansion later converted into a public house within historic Allerton parkland.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Blickling Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Blickling Hall is a Jacobean stately home situated in 5,000 acres (2,000 ha) of parkland in a loop of the River Bure, near the village of Blickling north of Aylsham in Norfolk, England. The mansion was built on the ruins of a Tudor building for Sir Henry Hobart from 1616 and designed by Robert Lyminge.
why_interesting: Jacobean mansion traditionally linked to Anne Boleyn, with an outstanding library and formal gardens.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Broughton Hall, Merseyside
Wikipedia Extract: Broughton Hall is a Gothic Revival house at Yew Tree Lane in West Derby, Liverpool, England. It was built in 1860 for Gustav Christian Schwabe, a Liverpool merchant originating from Hamburg, Germany.
why_interesting: Historic West Derby mansion now incorporated into the campus of Broughton Hall Catholic High School.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Bylaugh Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Bylaugh Hall, also known as Bylaugh Park, is a country house situated in the parish of Bylaugh in Norfolk, England.
why_interesting: Victorian mansion designed by Charles Barry Jr and Robert Richardson Banks, later rescued from severe dereliction.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Croxteth Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Croxteth Hall is a country estate and Grade II* listed building in the West Derby suburb of Liverpool, England. It is the former country estate and ancestral home of the Molyneux family, the Earls of Sefton.
why_interesting: Former seat of the Earls of Sefton, preserved with working estate buildings and Victorian farm attractions.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Felbrigg Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Felbrigg Hall is a 17th-century English country house near the village of that name in Norfolk. Part of a National Trust property, the unaltered 17th-century house is noted for its Jacobean architecture and fine Georgian interior.
why_interesting: Elegant country house with a notable library, stained glass and extensive parkland.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Holkham Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Holkham Hall ( or ) is an 18th-century country house near the village of Holkham, Norfolk, England, constructed in the Neo-Palladian style for Thomas Coke, 1st Earl of Leicester (of the fifth creation of the title). The hall was designed by the architect William Kent, with contributions from Richard Boyle, 3rd Earl of Burlington, the Norfolk architect and surveyor, Matthew Brettingham and Coke himself.
why_interesting: Palladian masterpiece built for the Coke family, surrounded by a vast working estate.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Houghton Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Houghton Hall ( HOW-tən) is a country house in the parish of Houghton in Norfolk, England. It is the residence of the 7th Marquess of Cholmondeley.
why_interesting: Grand Palladian house built for Robert Walpole, Britain's first prime minister, now showcasing contemporary sculpture.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Acklam Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Acklam Hall is a Restoration mansion in the former village, and now suburb, of Acklam in Middlesbrough, North Yorkshire, England. It is a Grade I listed building.
why_interesting: Middlesbrough's only Grade I-listed building, built in the 1680s for the Hustler family.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Aldby Park
Wikipedia Extract:
Aldby Park is a country estate in the village of Buttercrambe, near the village of Stamford Bridge in the East Riding of Yorkshire, England.
The house, replacing the original Tudor one, was built around 1725 by Jane Darley but it occupies an ancient site believed to be where Edwin of Northumbria was crowned King in 625 AD.
Aldby Park is best known as being the ancestral home of the Darley family.
why_interesting: Georgian country house standing in landscaped parkland beside the River Derwent.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Allerton Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Allerton Castle, also known as Allerton Park, is a Grade I listed nineteenth-century Gothic or Victorian Gothic house at Allerton Mauleverer in North Yorkshire, England. It was rebuilt by architect George Martin, of Baker Street, London in 1843–1853.
why_interesting: Dramatic Gothic Revival mansion dominated by one of England's grandest baronial halls.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Aske Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Aske Hall is a Georgian country house, with parkland attributed to Capability Brown, 1.5 miles (2.4 km) north of Richmond, North Yorkshire, England. It contains an impressive collection of 18th-century furniture, paintings and porcelain, and in its grounds a John Carr stable block converted into a chapel in Victorian times with Italianate decor, a Gothic-style folly built by Daniel Garrett circa 1745, coach house with carriage, Victorian stable block, walled garden, terraced garden and lake with a Roman-style temple.
why_interesting: Country seat of the Marquesses of Zetland, set within sweeping North Yorkshire parkland.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Bishopthorpe Palace
Wikipedia Extract: Bishopthorpe Palace is the official residence of the Archbishop of York at Bishopthorpe, North Yorkshire, England. The palace is located on the River Ouse and is approximately 3 miles (4.8 km) south of York, which is the location of the diocese's cathedral, York Minster.
why_interesting: Official residence of the Archbishop of York since the 13th century.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Duncombe Park
Wikipedia Extract: Duncombe Park is the seat of the Duncombe family who previously held the title Earls of Feversham. The title became extinct on the death of the 3rd Earl in 1963, since when the family have continued to hold the title Baron Feversham.
why_interesting: Baroque mansion above the Rye Valley, with terraces and a renowned birds-of-prey centre.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Farnley Hall, North Yorkshire
Wikipedia Extract: Farnley Hall is a stately home in Farnley, North Yorkshire, England. It is located near Otley.
why_interesting: Country house closely associated with J. M. W. Turner, who stayed and painted there repeatedly.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Fountains Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Fountains Hall is a country house near Ripon in North Yorkshire, England, located within the World Heritage Site at Studley Royal Park which include the ruins of Fountains Abbey. It belongs to the National Trust and is a Grade I listed building.
why_interesting: Jacobean mansion built partly from stone taken from the neighbouring ruins of Fountains Abbey.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Moulton Hall
Wikipedia Extract:
Moulton Hall is a grade I listed 17th-century manor house in Moulton near Richmond, North Yorkshire, England. 
The hall is built to a rectangular plan in three storeys with cellar and attics of ashlar and rubble with Westmorland slate roofs.
why_interesting: Seventeenth-century Jacobean manor preserved by the National Trust and long associated with the D'Arcy family.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Newburgh Priory
Wikipedia Extract:
Newburgh Priory is a Grade I listed Tudor building near Coxwold, North Yorkshire, England. 
Originally a house of Augustinian canons, it was founded in 1145 and became a family home following the dissolution of the priory in 1538.
why_interesting: Country house incorporating former priory buildings and linked to legends about Oliver Cromwell's missing remains.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Newby Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Newby Hall is a country house beside the River Ure in the parish of Skelton-on-Ure in North Yorkshire, England. It is 3 miles (4.8 km) south-east of Ripon and 6 miles (9.7 km) south of Topcliffe Castle, by which the manor of Newby was originally held.
why_interesting: Elegant 18th-century house celebrated for Robert Adam interiors, Chippendale furniture and extensive gardens.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Althorp
Wikipedia Extract: Althorp (popularly pronounced  AWL-thorp) is a Grade I listed stately home and estate in the civil parish of Althorp, in West Northamptonshire, England of about 13,000 acres (5,300 ha). By road it is about 6 miles (9.7 km) northwest of the county town of Northampton and about 75 miles (121 km) northwest of central London, situated between the villages of Great Brington and Harlestone.
why_interesting: Spencer family seat for over five centuries and the childhood home of Diana, Princess of Wales.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Castle Howard
Wikipedia Extract: Castle Howard railway station was a minor railway station serving the village of Welburn and the stately home at Castle Howard in North Yorkshire, England. On the York to Scarborough Line it was opened on 5 July 1845 by the York and North Midland Railway.
why_interesting: Baroque masterpiece designed by Vanbrugh and Hawksmoor, taking more than a century to complete.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Stanwick Park
Wikipedia Extract: Stanwick Park (also known as Stanwick Hall) was a Palladian country house at Stanwick St John in North Yorkshire, England.
why_interesting: Former Smithson family estate whose mansion was demolished, leaving historic parkland and archaeological traces.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Barnwell Manor
Wikipedia Extract: Barnwell Manor is a Grade II listed country estate near the village of Barnwell, about 2.5 miles (4.0 km) south of Oundle, in Northamptonshire, England. The historic former home of the Duke and Duchess of Gloucester, and subsequently the home of Windsor House Antiques, in September 2022, Prince Richard, Duke of Gloucester, put the manor up for sale for £4.75 million  and it was sold in April 2024.
why_interesting: Country house beside medieval Barnwell Castle, formerly home to the Duke and Duchess of Gloucester.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Brockhall, Northamptonshire
Wikipedia Extract: Brockhall is a civil parish and village in West Northamptonshire in England. Brockhall, like many estate villages, is a small settlement that has developed around its eponymous hall.
why_interesting: Elegant Georgian country house set in Northamptonshire parkland, with origins reaching back to the 17th century.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Canons Ashby House
Wikipedia Extract: Canons Ashby House (previously known as Canons Ashby Hall) is a Grade I listed Elizabethan manor house located in the village of Canons Ashby, about 11 miles (17.7 km) south of the town of Daventry in the county of Northamptonshire, England. It has been owned by the National Trust since 1981 when the house was close to collapse and the gardens had turned into a meadow.
why_interesting: Tudor manor preserved by the National Trust, with historic interiors, formal gardens and strong Dryden family connections.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Cosgrove Hall, Northamptonshire
Wikipedia Extract: Cosgrove Hall is an early-18th-century Grade II listed country house in Cosgrove, Northamptonshire. It was built on the site of an earlier house by the Furtho family.
why_interesting: Former Northamptonshire country house overlooking the Great Ouse valley, later lost after wartime decline.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Blanchland Abbey
Wikipedia Extract: Blanchland Abbey at Blanchland, in the English county of Northumberland, was founded as a premonstratensian priory in 1165 by Walter de Bolbec II, and was a daughter house of Croxton Abbey in Leicestershire. It became an abbey in the late 13th century.
why_interesting: Premonstratensian abbey remains woven into a picturesque stone village built largely from monastic fabric.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Capheaton Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Capheaton Hall, near Wallington, Northumberland, is an English country house, the seat of the Swinburne Baronets and a childhood home of the poet Algernon Swinburne.  It counts among the principal gentry seats of Northumberland.
why_interesting: Baroque country house built in the 17th century and set within landscaped Northumberland parkland.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Churnsike Lodge
Wikipedia Extract: Churnsike Lodge is an early Victorian hunting lodge situated in the parish of Greystead, west Northumberland, England. Constructed in 1850 by the Charlton family, descendants of the noted Border Reivers family of the English Middle March, the lodge formed part of the extensive Hesleyside estate, located some 10 miles from Hesleyside Hall itself.
why_interesting: Remote Northumberland hunting lodge surrounded by the wild forests and moorland of the Border country.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Cragside
Wikipedia Extract: Cragside is a Tudor Revival country house near the town of Rothbury in Northumberland, England. Dating to the Victorian era, it was the home of William Armstrong, 1st Baron Armstrong, founder of the Armstrong Whitworth armaments firm.
why_interesting: Victorian home of inventor William Armstrong and the first house in the world lit by hydroelectricity.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Annesley Hall, Nottinghamshire
Wikipedia Extract: Annesley Hall is a Grade II listed country house near Annesley in Nottinghamshire, England and the ancestral home of the Chaworth-Musters family. The 13th-century park, 17th-century terraces and 19th-century pleasure gardens and walled gardens of the hall are Grade II* listed on the Register of Historic Parks and Gardens.
why_interesting: Ruined ancestral home of the Chaworth family, remembered for its close associations with Lord Byron.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Ashdown House, Oxfordshire
Wikipedia Extract: Ashdown House (also known as Ashdown Park) is a 17th-century country house in the civil parish of Ashbury in the English county of Oxfordshire. Until 1974 the house was in the county of Berkshire, and the nearby village of Lambourn remains in that county.
why_interesting: Distinctive Dutch-style house built for Elizabeth of Bohemia, although she died before seeing it completed.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Beaumont Palace
Wikipedia Extract: Beaumont Palace, built outside the north gate of Oxford, was intended by Henry I about 1130 to serve as a royal palace conveniently close to the royal hunting-lodge at Woodstock (now part of the park of Blenheim Palace). Its former presence is recorded in Beaumont Street, Oxford.
why_interesting: Lost royal palace where Richard the Lionheart and King John were both born.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Beckett Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Beckett Hall (or Beckett House) is a country house at Shrivenham in the English county of Oxfordshire (formerly in Berkshire). The present house dates from 1831.
why_interesting: Historic country house long associated with the Barrington family and later absorbed into a military estate.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Chastleton House
Wikipedia Extract: Chastleton House () is a Jacobean country house at Chastleton, Oxfordshire, England, close to Moreton-in-Marsh (grid reference SP2429). It has been owned by the National Trust since 1991 and is a Grade I listed building.
why_interesting: Remarkably preserved Jacobean house whose faded interiors create an unusually authentic historic time capsule.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Cogges Manor Farm
Wikipedia Extract: Cogges Manor Farm is a one-time working farm in Cogges near Witney in Oxfordshire, England, now a heritage centre operated by a charitable trust and open to the public.
why_interesting: Historic Oxfordshire farmstead used as Yew Tree Farm in the television drama Downton Abbey.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Crocker End House
Wikipedia Extract: Crocker End House in Nettlebed in Henley-on-Thames, Oxfordshire, England is a spacious Victorian home built to replace Nettlebed's prosperous rectory in about 1870.  It was bought by the Duke and Duchess of Kent in December 1989.
why_interesting: Secluded Oxfordshire country house noted for its traditional architecture and wooded Chiltern setting.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Attingham Park
Wikipedia Extract: Attingham Park  is an English country house and estate in Shropshire located near the village of Atcham, on the B4380 Shrewsbury to Wellington road. It is owned by the National Trust and is a Grade I listed building.
why_interesting: Regency mansion with interiors by John Nash, surrounded by an extensive Repton-designed landscape.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Benthall Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Benthall Hall is a 16th-century English country house in Benthall in the town of Broseley, Shropshire, England, and a few miles from the historic Ironbridge Gorge. It retains much of its fine oak interior, and an elaborate 17th-century staircase.
why_interesting: Sixteenth-century stone manor with Catholic family history and scars from the English Civil War.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Boscobel House
Wikipedia Extract: Boscobel House (grid reference SJ837082) is a Grade II* listed building in the parish of Boscobel in Shropshire. It has been, at various times, a farmhouse, a hunting lodge, and a holiday home; but it is most famous for its role in the escape of Charles II after the Battle of Worcester in 1651.
why_interesting: Charles II famously hid in an oak tree here after defeat at the Battle of Worcester.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Condover Hall
Wikipedia Extract:
Condover Hall is a Grade I listed three-storey Elizabethan sandstone building, described as the grandest manor house in Shropshire, standing in a conservation area on the outskirts of Condover village, Shropshire, England, four miles south of the county town of Shrewsbury.
A Royal manor in Anglo Saxon times, until the 16th century Condover Manor was in and out of Crown Tenure.
why_interesting: Grand Elizabethan mansion attributed to John Thorpe, now used as a residential activity centre.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Ashton Court
Wikipedia Extract: Ashton Court is a mansion house and estate to the west of Bristol in England. Although the estate lies mainly in North Somerset, it is owned by the City of Bristol.
why_interesting: Historic Bristol estate with a deer park that hosts the city's internationally known balloon fiesta.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Barrington Court
Wikipedia Extract:
Barrington Court is a Tudor manor house begun around 1538 and completed in the late 1550s, with a vernacular stable court (1675), situated in Barrington, near Ilminster, Somerset, England.
The house was owned by several families by 1745 after which it fell into disrepair and was used as a tenant farm.
why_interesting: Fine Tudor manor and the first large country house acquired by the National Trust.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Barwick, Somerset
Wikipedia Extract: Barwick is a village and parish in Somerset, England, about 2 miles (3.2 km) south of Yeovil and on the border with Dorset. The parish, which includes the village of Stoford, has a population of 1,221.
why_interesting: Somerset estate best known for Barwick Park's four eccentric 18th-century follies.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Brympton d'Evercy
Wikipedia Extract: Brympton d'Evercy (alternatively Brympton House) is a Grade I listed manor house near Yeovil in the county of Somerset, England. The house has been called the most beautiful of its kind in England; in 1927, Christopher Hussey, near the start of a 50-year career as an architectural authority, termed it "the one which created the greatest impression and summarises so exquisitely English country life qualities." The house has belonged to six families since its construction: the D'Evercys, Stourtons, Sydenhams, Fanes, Weeks (1992–2008), and Glossops (since 2008).
why_interesting: Architecturally rich medieval manor often praised as one of England's most beautiful country houses.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Clevedon Court
Wikipedia Extract: Clevedon Court is a manor house on Court Hill in Clevedon, North Somerset, England, dating from the early 14th century. It is owned by the National Trust and is designated as a Grade I listed building.
why_interesting: Rare medieval manor house with a 14th-century core, historic interiors and terraced gardens.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Cricket St Thomas
Wikipedia Extract:
Cricket St Thomas is a parish in Somerset, England, situated in a valley between Chard and Crewkerne and was formerly within the South Somerset administrative district.
The A30 road passes nearby.
why_interesting: Somerset estate widely recognised as the setting for the television comedy To the Manor Born.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Bishops' House
Wikipedia Extract: Bishops' House is a half-timbered house in Norton Lees, a suburban area of  Sheffield, England. It was built c. 1500 and is located on the southern tip of Meersbrook Park.
why_interesting: One of Sheffield's oldest surviving buildings, preserving a rare timber-framed Tudor house.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Brodsworth Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Brodsworth Hall, near Brodsworth, 5 miles (8 km) north-west of Doncaster in South Yorkshire, is one of the most complete surviving examples of a Victorian country house in England. It is virtually unchanged since the 1860s.
why_interesting: Victorian country house preserved largely as its last family left it, with restored formal gardens.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Burntwood Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Burntwood Hall is a house that lies near the village of Great Houghton, South Yorkshire, England and has been known as Boomshack and Burntwood Nook/Lodge over the centuries.
why_interesting: Historic South Yorkshire country house surrounded by former estate parkland near Barnsley.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Cannon Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Cannon Hall is a country house museum located between the villages of Cawthorne and High Hoyland some 5 miles (8 km) west of Barnsley, South Yorkshire, England.  Originally the home of the Spencer and later the Spencer-Stanhope family, it now houses collections of fine furniture, paintings, ceramics and glassware.
why_interesting: Georgian country house museum displaying decorative arts, ceramics and local history collections.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Alton Towers
Wikipedia Extract: Alton Towers (UK:   OL-tən) (also known as Alton Towers Resort) is a historic estate, theme park and resort complex in Staffordshire, England, near the village of Alton. The park is operated by Merlin Entertainments Group and incorporates a theme park, water park, mini golf and hotel complex.
why_interesting: Ruined Gothic Revival mansion whose former estate developed into one of Britain's largest theme parks.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Biddulph Grange
Wikipedia Extract: Biddulph Grange is a National Trust landscaped garden, in Biddulph near Stoke-on-Trent, Staffordshire, England. It is separate from Biddulph Grange Country Park.
why_interesting: Extraordinary Victorian garden arranged as a journey through China, Egypt, Italy and other world landscapes.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Blithfield Hall
Wikipedia Extract:
Blithfield Hall (pronounced locally as Bliffield), is a privately owned Grade I listed country house in Staffordshire, England, situated some 9 miles (14 km) east of Stafford, 7 miles (11 km) southwest of Uttoxeter and 5 miles (8.0 km) north of Rugeley.

The Hall, with its embattled towers and walls, has been the home of the Bagot family since the late 14th century.
why_interesting: Historic seat of the Bagot family, combining Tudor origins with later Gothic additions.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Chillington Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Chillington Hall is a Georgian country house near Brewood, Staffordshire, England, four miles northwest of Wolverhampton. It is the residence of the Giffard family.
why_interesting: Elegant Georgian mansion designed partly by Sir John Soane and set in Capability Brown parkland.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Drayton Manor
Wikipedia Extract: Drayton Manor, one of Britain's lost houses, was a British stately home at Drayton Bassett, since its formation in the District of Lichfield, Staffordshire, England. In modern administrative areas, it was first put into Tamworth Poor Law Union and similar Rural Sanitary District, 1894 to 1934 saw its inclusion in Tamworth Rural District, and in the next forty years it lay in the Lichfield Rural District (which was abolished in 1974).
why_interesting: Former Peel family country estate, now better known as the site of Drayton Manor theme park.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Etruria Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Etruria Hall in Etruria, Stoke-on-Trent, Staffordshire, England is a Grade II listed house and former home of the potter Josiah Wedgwood. It was built between 1768–1771 by Joseph Pickford.
why_interesting: Josiah Wedgwood's former home, built beside the pioneering pottery works he established at Etruria.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Christchurch Mansion
Wikipedia Extract: Christchurch Mansion is a substantial Tudor brick mansion house built in Ipswich, Suffolk, England, by Edmund Withypoll (also written "Withipoll") around 1548–1550. The Grade I listed building is located within Christchurch Park and sits by the southern gates close to the town centre of Ipswich.
why_interesting: Tudor mansion housing notable collections of fine art, including works by Constable and Gainsborough.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Culford Park
Wikipedia Extract: Culford Park in Culford, Suffolk, England, is a country house that is the former seat of the Bacon, Cornwallis and Cadogan families, and now the home of Culford School.
why_interesting: Grand Suffolk country house set in landscaped parkland and now forming the centrepiece of Culford School.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Desning Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Desning Hall was a manor house in Dalham, Risbridge Hundred, in Suffolk, England, dating from Anglo-Saxon times. Desning Hall's last resident was Sidney Arthur King who left the property in 1927.
why_interesting: Historic Suffolk manor house representing the long-established rural estates of the Newmarket countryside.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Euston Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Euston Hall is a country house, with park by William Kent and Capability Brown, in Euston, a small village in Suffolk, England, just south of Thetford. It is the family home of the Dukes of Grafton.
why_interesting: Country seat of the Dukes of Grafton, surrounded by historic parkland shaped by Capability Brown.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Helmingham Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Helmingham Hall is a moated manor house in Helmingham, Suffolk, England. It was begun by John Tollemache in 1480 and has been owned by the Tollemache family ever since.
why_interesting: Moated Tudor hall where the drawbridges are still traditionally raised each night.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Bagshot Park
Wikipedia Extract: Bagshot Park is a royal residence located near Bagshot, a village 11 miles (18 km) south of Windsor. It is on Bagshot Heath, a 50-square-mile (130 km2) tract of formerly open land in Surrey and Berkshire.
why_interesting: Royal country residence built in the 19th century within extensive Surrey parkland.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Cherkley Court
Wikipedia Extract: Cherkley Court, at the extreme southeast of Leatherhead, Surrey, in England, is a late Victorian neo-classical mansion and estate of 370 acres (1.5 km2), once the home of Canadian-born press baron Lord Beaverbrook. The main house is listed Grade II on the National Heritage List for England.
why_interesting: Former home of newspaper magnate Lord Beaverbrook, now part of an exclusive country estate.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Clandon Park House
Wikipedia Extract:
Clandon Park House is an early 18th-century grade I listed Palladian mansion in West Clandon, near Guildford in Surrey.
It stands in the south east corner of Clandon Park, a 220-hectare (540-acre) agricultural parkland estate which has been the seat of the Earls of Onslow for over two centuries.
why_interesting: Palladian mansion severely damaged by fire in 2015, leaving a major conservation and restoration challenge.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Claremont (country house)
Wikipedia Extract: Claremont, also known historically as 'Clermont', is an 18th-century Palladian mansion less than a mile south of the centre of Esher in Surrey, England. The buildings are now occupied by Claremont Fan Court School, and its landscaped gardens are owned and managed by the National Trust.
why_interesting: Historic royal residence associated with Princess Charlotte and surrounded by an influential landscape garden.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Deepdene House and Gardens
Wikipedia Extract: Deepdene was an estate and country house occupying land to the southeast of Dorking, Surrey, England. The remains of the gardens are Grade II* listed with the adjoining Chart Park on the Register of Historic Parks and Gardens.
why_interesting: Lost country house remembered through restored gardens, woodland trails and the Hope family mausoleum.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Eastley End House
Wikipedia Extract: Eastley End House is a Georgian house at the edge of the developed part of Thorpe, Surrey. It is a Grade II listed building, and was formerly part of the headquarters of RMC Group, a division of Cemex.
why_interesting: Private Surrey country house set within wooded grounds near the historic village of Thorpe.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Arbury Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Arbury Hall is a Grade I listed  country house in Nuneaton, Warwickshire, England, and the ancestral home of the Newdigate family, later the Newdigate-Newdegate and Fitzroy-Newdegate (Viscount Daventry) families.
why_interesting: Gothic Revival mansion and ancestral home of the Newdigate family, set on George Eliot's birthplace estate.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Baddesley Clinton
Wikipedia Extract: Baddesley Clinton is a moated manor house, about 8 miles (13 km) north-west of the town of Warwick, in the village of Baddesley Clinton, Warwickshire, England. The house probably originated in the 13th century, when large areas of the Forest of Arden were cleared for farmland.
why_interesting: Moated Tudor manor famed for concealed priest holes used during periods of Catholic persecution.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Gibside
Wikipedia Extract: Gibside is an estate in Tyne and Wear, England. It is located in the valley of the River Derwent on the border with County Durham, between Rowlands Gill and Burnopfield.
why_interesting: Atmospheric Georgian landscape with a ruined mansion, Palladian chapel and sweeping views over the Derwent Valley.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Hatchlands Park
Wikipedia Extract: Hatchlands Park is a country house in East Clandon, Surrey, in the care of the National Trust. Unusually, the house is tenanted to the Cobbe family, whose collection furnishes it.
why_interesting: Georgian mansion containing the Cobbe Collection, one of the world's largest groups of historic keyboard instruments.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Castle Bromwich Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Castle Bromwich Hall is a Jacobean mansion in the Castle Bromwich area of Solihull, England.  It is a Grade I listed building.
why_interesting: Jacobean mansion beside exceptionally well-preserved formal gardens, now operating as a hotel.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Charlecote Park
Wikipedia Extract: Charlecote Park is a grand 16th-century country house, surrounded by its own deer park, on the banks of the River Avon in Charlecote near Wellesbourne, about 4 miles (6 km) east of Stratford-upon-Avon and 5.5 miles (9 km) south of Warwick in Warwickshire, England. It has been administered by the National Trust since 1946.
why_interesting: Tudor house and deer park associated with the Lucy family and a famous Shakespeare poaching legend.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Compton Wynyates
Wikipedia Extract: Compton Wynyates is a Tudor country house in Warwickshire, England, a Grade I listed building. The Tudor period house is constructed of red brick and built around a central courtyard.
why_interesting: Romantic moated Tudor manor distinguished by clustered chimneys, courtyards and largely unaltered architecture.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Coombe Abbey
Wikipedia Extract: Coombe Abbey (also Combe Abbey) is a former Cistercian abbey at Combe Fields in the Borough of Rugby, in the countryside of Warwickshire, England. The abbey was converted to a  country house in the 16th century and now operates as a hotel.
why_interesting: Former Cistercian abbey transformed into a grand country house and later a hotel.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Coughton Court
Wikipedia Extract: Coughton Court () is an English Tudor country house, situated on the main road between Studley and Alcester in Warwickshire. It is a Grade I listed building.
why_interesting: Throckmorton family home with strong Catholic history and close connections to the Gunpowder Plot.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Great Barr Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Great Barr Hall is an 18th-century mansion situated in the Great Barr district of Pheasey, historically in Staffordshire and now part of Walsall, West Midlands, England. It has associations with the Lunar Society and is a Grade II listed building.
why_interesting: Ruined country house whose estate became associated with members of Birmingham's influential Lunar Society.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Becca Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Becca Hall is a country residence situated in Aberford, Leeds, West Yorkshire, Yorkshire, at OS grid reference Lat.53:50:35N Lon.1:22:08W. It is situated on Becca Lane within the old Gascoigne estate. The house is a Grade II listed building.
why_interesting: Former 18th-century country house near Aberford, demolished in the 20th century but remembered through its estate.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Brantridge Park
Wikipedia Extract: Brantridge Park, Balcombe, West Sussex, England is a 19th-century country house, formerly one of the lesser royal residences. It is a Grade II listed building.
why_interesting: Former royal residence associated with Princess Alice, Countess of Athlone, during the 20th century.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Bretton Hall, West Yorkshire
Wikipedia Extract: Bretton Hall is a country house in West Bretton near Wakefield, West Yorkshire, England. It housed Bretton Hall College from 1949 until 2001 and was a campus of the University of Leeds from 2001 to 2007.
why_interesting: Eighteenth-century mansion now forming the historic heart of Yorkshire Sculpture Park.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Bowood House
Wikipedia Extract: Bowood is a Grade I listed Georgian country house in Wiltshire, England, that has been owned for more than 250 years by the Fitzmaurice family. The house, with interiors by Robert Adam, stands in extensive grounds which include a garden designed by Lancelot "Capability" Brown.
why_interesting: Lansdowne family seat where Joseph Priestley discovered oxygen, set within Capability Brown parkland.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Corsham Court
Wikipedia Extract: Corsham Court is a 16th-century country house in a park designed by Capability Brown.  It is in the town of Corsham, 3 miles (5 km) west of Chippenham, Wiltshire, and is notable for its fine art collection, based on the nucleus of paintings inherited in 1757 by Paul Methuen from his uncle, Sir Paul Methuen, the diplomat.
why_interesting: Elizabethan country house celebrated for its important art collection and centuries of Methuen family history.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Great Chalfield Manor
Wikipedia Extract: Great Chalfield Manor is an English country house at Great Chalfield, about 2.5 miles (4 km) northeast of the town of Bradford on Avon in the west of the county of Wiltshire.
why_interesting: Late-medieval moated manor celebrated for its romantic Arts and Crafts garden and beautifully preserved interiors.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Hartham Park
Wikipedia Extract: Hartham Park is a Georgian manor house in Wiltshire, England, about 1+1⁄4 miles (2.0 km) north of the town of Corsham. Originally designed by James Wyatt, and set today in 50 acres (20 ha), it has within its grounds a stické tennis court.
why_interesting: Georgian mansion set in historic Wiltshire parkland, later adapted as a modern business estate.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Littlecote House
Wikipedia Extract: Littlecote House is a large Elizabethan country house and estate in the civil parishes of Ramsbury and Chilton Foliat, in the English county of Wiltshire, about 2+1⁄2 miles (4 km) northeast of the Berkshire town of Hungerford. The estate includes 34 hectares of historic parklands and gardens, including a walled garden dating from the 17th and 18th centuries.
why_interesting: Tudor manor linked to royal visits, Civil War history and an exceptional Roman mosaic.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Longleat
Wikipedia Extract: Longleat is a stately home about 4 miles (7 km) west of Warminster in Wiltshire, England. A leading and early example of the Elizabethan prodigy house, it is a Grade I listed building and the seat of the Marquesses of Bath.
why_interesting: Elizabethan prodigy house whose estate opened Britain's first drive-through safari park outside Africa.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Barnt Green House
Wikipedia Extract: Barnt Green House is a building at Barnt Green, Worcestershire, England. It is a Grade II listed building.
why_interesting: Historic Worcestershire country house associated with Barnt Green's growth as a prosperous rural and commuter settlement.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Birtsmorton Court
Wikipedia Extract:
Birtsmorton Court is a Grade I listed fortified medieval moated manor house near Malvern in Worcestershire, in the former woodlands of Malvern Chase.
It is located in Birtsmorton, a small agricultural parish 7 miles south-east of Malvern Wells, Worcestershire and 8 miles west of Tewkesbury, Gloucestershire.
why_interesting: Atmospheric moated manor with medieval origins, timber-framed buildings and beautifully preserved courtyards.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Chateau Impney
Wikipedia Extract: Chateau Impney Hotel & Exhibition Centre is a Grade II* listed 19th-century house built in the style of an elaborate French château near Droitwich Spa in Worcestershire, England. Of the large mansions in Worcestershire supported by industrial fortunes, Sir Nicolas Pevsner judged Impney to be "the showiest of them all in the county".
why_interesting: French château-style mansion built in the 1870s by salt magnate John Corbett for his French wife.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Hanbury Hall
Wikipedia Extract: Hanbury Hall is a large 18th-century stately home standing in parkland at Hanbury, Worcestershire. The main range has two storeys and is built of red brick in the Queen Anne style.
why_interesting: Queen Anne country house noted for James Thornhill's staircase paintings and restored formal gardens.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Hewell Grange
Wikipedia Extract: Hewell Grange is a former country house in Tardebigge, Worcestershire, England. "One of the most important late 19th century country houses in England", the mansion was built between 1884 and 1891 by George Frederick Bodley and Thomas Garner for Robert Windsor-Clive, later first Earl of Plymouth.
why_interesting: Grand Gothic Revival mansion later incorporated into a prison complex.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Birkhall
Wikipedia Extract: Birkhall (from the Scots Birk Hauch: "Birch River-meadow") is a 210 km2 (52,000 acres) estate on Royal Deeside, Aberdeenshire, Scotland, owned by King Charles III. It is located alongside the River Muick to the south-west of Ballater.
why_interesting: Royal residence on the Balmoral estate, closely associated with Queen Elizabeth The Queen Mother.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Abbotsford, Scottish Borders
Wikipedia Extract: Abbotsford is a historic country house in the Scottish Borders, near Galashiels, on the south bank of the River Tweed. Now open to the public, it was built as the residence of historical novelist and poet Sir Walter Scott between 1817 and 1825.
why_interesting: Sir Walter Scott's extraordinary baronial home, filled with his books, armour and personal collections.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Craigdarroch
Wikipedia Extract:
"Craigdarroch, An Accessory to Murder" is an expansion set for the board game Kill Doctor Lucky

Craigdarroch is a house near Moniaive, Dumfries and Galloway, Scotland. It was the seat of the Chief of the Dumfriesshire Fergussons for 600 years.
why_interesting: Historic Dumfriesshire country estate set amid the wooded landscape of the Cairn Valley.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Craigenputtock
Wikipedia Extract: Craigenputtock (usually spelled by the Carlyles as Craigenputtoch) is a farmhouse in Scotland where Thomas Carlyle lived from 1828 to 1834.  He wrote several of his early works there, including Sartor Resartus.
why_interesting: Remote farmhouse where Thomas Carlyle wrote much of Sartor Resartus during the 1830s.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Auchinleck House
Wikipedia Extract: Auchinleck House is an 18th-century mansion in Scotland. It is situated near the town of Auchinleck near Cumnock and Ayr in East Ayrshire.
why_interesting: Palladian Boswell family mansion associated with diarist James Boswell and restored by the Landmark Trust.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Callendar House
Wikipedia Extract: Callendar House is a mansion set within the grounds of Callendar Park in Falkirk, central Scotland. During the 19th century, it was redesigned and extended in the style of a French Renaissance château fused with elements of Scottish baronial architecture.
why_interesting: Historic mansion with connections to Mary, Queen of Scots and the Civil Wars, now housing a local museum.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Gosford House
Wikipedia Extract:
Gosford House is a neoclassical country house around 2 miles (3 km) northeast of Longniddry in East Lothian, Scotland, on the A198 Aberlady Road, in 5,000 acres (2,000 ha) of parkland and coast.
It is the family seat of the Charteris family, the Earls of Wemyss and March.
why_interesting: Robert Adam-designed neoclassical mansion distinguished by a spectacular marble hall.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Cambusnethan House
Wikipedia Extract: Cambusnethan House, or Cambusnethan Priory, in North Lanarkshire, Scotland, was designed by James Gillespie Graham and completed in 1820. It is listed on the Buildings at Risk Register for Scotland as a building facing "critical" risk, having been damaged by fire in the 1980s and since vandalized.
why_interesting: Ruined early-19th-century Gothic Revival mansion overlooking the Clyde Valley.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Cawdor Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Cawdor Castle is a castle in the parish of Cawdor in Nairnshire, Scotland. It is built around a 15th-century tower house, with substantial additions in later centuries.
why_interesting: Picturesque medieval castle linked to Macbeth, although the present building postdates him by centuries.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Colzium
Wikipedia Extract: Colzium House and Estate (pronounced Coal-Zee-Um) is about 500 metres to the north-east of Kilsyth, North Lanarkshire, Scotland. The present house dates from 1783 and was extended and modernised in 1861.
why_interesting: Eighteenth-century mansion set within parkland near the site of the Battle of Kilsyth.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Amhuinnsuidhe Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Amhuinnsuidhe Castle is a large 19th-century private country house on Harris, one of the Western Isles of Scotland. It was designated as a Category A listed building in 1971 and is now operated as a hotel and shooting estate.
why_interesting: Scottish Baronial castle commanding a dramatic shoreline setting on the Isle of Harris.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Corehouse
Wikipedia Extract: Corehouse is a country house and estate, located 2 kilometres (1.2 mi) to the south of Lanark, Scotland. The estate is by the Corra Linn Falls on the River Clyde, and close to the World Heritage Site of New Lanark.
why_interesting: Early-19th-century country house overlooking the dramatic Falls of Clyde.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Ayr Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Ayr Castle was a castle situated at Ayr in Scotland. Once considered a royal castle, nothing remains of it above ground.
why_interesting: Site of Ayr's vanished medieval castle rather than a surviving stately home.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Brahan Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Brahan Castle was situated 3.5 miles (5.6 km) south-west of Dingwall, in Easter Ross, Highland Scotland. The castle belonged to the Earls of Seaforth, chiefs of the Clan Mackenzie, who dominated the area.
why_interesting: Demolished ancestral seat of the Earls of Seaforth, linked to the legendary Brahan Seer.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Cathcart Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Cathcart Castle was a 15th-century castle, located in what is now Linn Park in the Cathcart area of southern Glasgow, Scotland. The castle was abandoned in the 18th century, and the remaining ruins were pulled down in 1980, leaving only foundations visible.
why_interesting: Ruined medieval stronghold overlooking the area associated with the Battle of Langside.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Ackergill Tower
Wikipedia Extract: Ackergill Tower (or Ackergill Castle) is located on the coast of Sinclair's Bay, about 2.5 miles (4.0 km) north of Wick, Caithness, in northern Scotland. It was built in the early 16th century, and is a Category A listed building.
why_interesting: Fifteenth-century coastal tower house shaped by the long-running feud between the Keith and Sinclair clans.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Bishop's Castle, Glasgow
Wikipedia Extract: The Bishop's Castle (also known as Glasgow Castle, the Bishop's Palace, and the Archbishop's Palace) was a medieval castle in the district of Townhead, Glasgow, Scotland. It stood to the west of Glasgow Cathedral, covering much of the present day Cathedral Square.
why_interesting: Site of Glasgow's medieval episcopal castle, once standing beside the cathedral.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Castle Holydean
Wikipedia Extract:
Holydean Castle (pronounced "hollydeen") was a castle sited near Melrose in Bowden, 1.25 miles SW of the village, in the Scottish Borders region of Scotland, and the former Roxburghshire.
The castle was founded by King David I. It was destroyed in 1276, rebuilt in 1530 by Dame Ker, and destroyed again by the 3rd Duke of Roxburghe in 1760.
why_interesting: Ruined 16th-century tower house once held by the powerful Kerr family.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Jedburgh Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Jedburgh Castle was a castle at Jedburgh in Scotland. It was fought over during the Wars of Scottish Independence, and was demolished by the Scots commanded by Sir James Douglas of Balvenie in 1409.
why_interesting: Former royal castle site now occupied by a distinctive 19th-century jail museum.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Kilravock Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Kilravock Castle (pronounced Kilrawk) is located near the village of Croy, between Inverness and Nairn, in the council area of Highland, Scotland. It was begun around 1460 and has been the seat of the Clan Rose since that time.
why_interesting: Castle occupied by the Rose family for roughly 750 years, combining a medieval tower with later additions.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Kinloch Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Kinloch Castle (Scottish Gaelic: Caisteal Cheann Locha) is an Edwardian mansion located on Kinloch, on the island of Rùm, one of the Small Isles off the west coast of Scotland. It was built as a private residence for Sir George Bullough, a textile tycoon from Lancashire whose father bought Rùm as his summer residence and shooting estate.
why_interesting: Remarkably intact Victorian mansion on Rum, preserving lavish interiors commissioned by industrialist George Bullough.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Newark Castle, Port Glasgow
Wikipedia Extract: Newark Castle is a well-preserved castle sited on the south shore of the estuary of the River Clyde in Port Glasgow, Inverclyde, Scotland, where the firth gradually narrows from the Firth of Clyde and navigation upriver is made difficult by shifting sandbanks. For centuries this location was used to offload seagoing ships, and led to the growth of Port Glasgow close to the castle on either side and to the south.
why_interesting: Renaissance mansion beside the Clyde, combining a medieval tower house with elegant 16th-century additions.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Belltrees Peel
Wikipedia Extract: Belltrees Peel is a medieval tower situated on a peninsula in Castle Semple Loch in Renfrewshire, Scotland, on which was once an island.
why_interesting: Rare surviving Scottish defensive tower dating from a turbulent period.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Broomhall Castle
Wikipedia Extract: Broomhall Castle is a mansion house originally called Broom Hall and was built in 1874 by John Foukes and Frances Mackison for James Johnstone. It is situated in Menstrie, Clackmannanshire, Scotland on the Ochil Hills and comprises three storeys and a tower.
why_interesting: Victorian Scottish Baronial mansion beneath the Ochil Hills, later converted for hospitality use.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Bonnington Pavilion
Wikipedia Extract: The Bonnington Pavilion or Hall of Mirrors, now a ruin, is situated in the grounds of the old estate of Bonnington, near New Lanark, overlooking Corra Linn falls on the River Clyde in Lanarkshire, Scotland. Alternative names are the Corra Linn Pavilion and the Falls of Clyde summerhouse.
why_interesting: Classical pavilion built as a viewpoint above the spectacular Falls of Clyde.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Fergushill
Wikipedia Extract: Fergushill is a small community in North Ayrshire, Parish of Kilwinning, Scotland. The Barony of Fergushill was held by the Fergushill family of that Ilk and the area has a complex history.
why_interesting: Former Ayrshire estate whose mansion has disappeared, leaving traces in the surrounding landscape.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Largie Castle, Tayinloan
Wikipedia Extract: Largie Castle is a former mansion house at Tayinloan, Kintyre, Argyll and Bute, Scotland. It was designed by architect Charles Wilson for The Hon.
why_interesting: Lost Kintyre castle once standing near Tayinloan, demolished during the 20th century.
Good For: history lovers, couples, family, day trip

name: Balruddery
Wikipedia Extract: Balruddery House by Longforgan in Perthshire, Scotland, was designed by David Neave for James Webster circa 1820. In about 1879 it was bought by James F White, who had previously leased Castle Huntly in Longforgan.
why_interesting: Historic Angus country estate associated with generations of rural landownership.
